title: Rethinking Time Series Tokenization from a Frequency Perspective
summary: Tokenization that partitions time series into subsequences has become a foundational paradigm in modern time series modeling. However, we find that current tokenization strategies inherently introduce spectral distortions, forcing the learned representations to diverge from the true underlying patterns such as trend, periodicity, and seasonality, thereby impairing model performance. Through theoretical analysis from a frequency perspective, we derive the boundary conditions under which such distortions occur. To overcome this distortion, we propose TimeFT, a nearly distortion-free frequency-based tokenizer for time series data. TimeFT obtains tokens through frequency-domain partitioning, frequency shifting, and Nyquist sampling. The method is parameter-free, incurs negligible computational complexity, and can serve as a drop-in replacement for existing tokenizers. Our extensive experiments on diverse tasks such as forecasting, classification, and anomaly detection demonstrate that TimeFT consistently and significantly improves performance.
core_methodology: TimeFT, a frequency-based tokenizer for time series data that avoids spectral distortions through frequency-domain partitioning, frequency shifting, and Nyquist sampling. It is parameter-free and computationally efficient.
data_sources: Time series data, which is fundamental in financial markets for price, volume, and other market metrics.
alpha_potential: The method improves the accuracy of time series modeling by preserving true underlying patterns such as trends and seasonality, which are crucial for forecasting financial time series, detecting anomalies, and classifying market regimes.
title_cn: 从频率视角重新思考时间序列的切分
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的时间序列切分方法TimeFT，通过频率域分割避免传统方法引入的频谱失真，显著提升了时间序列建模的准确性。在金融应用中，这可以改善价格预测、市场分类和异常检测，具有直接的交易策略优化潜力。

title: Understanding the Inner Workings of a State-Space Foundation Model for Limit Order Books
summary: Autoregressive foundation models offer state-of-the-art capabilities to simulate the market by generating the message flow of limit order books (LOBs). Yet, without understanding their inner workings, research directions are hard to narrow and practical use in real-world trading environments remains uncertain. This study therefore asks what these models actually learn about market microstructure. We find that, similarly to games where sequence models build an internal representation of the board, an 8.2M-parameter Mamba-3 state-space model trained autoregressively on the tokenized message stream of eight large-cap US equities learns an internal representation of the market and its dynamics. In particular, order-flow imbalance, a central driver of short-horizon price moves, is decodable at $R^2 \approx 0.59$, far above controls and baselines. This representation extends to unseen stocks, suggesting that these models learn general representations rather than ticker-specific patterns. The model also generalizes across metrics beyond order-flow imbalance: results hold across traded volume and volatility. Additionally, the representation is causally steerable: pushing the state along a feature's axis shifts the model's next-message beliefs as that feature implies, monotonically in dose, consistent with the emergence of a world model.
core_methodology: The paper employs an 8.2M-parameter Mamba-3 state-space model trained autoregressively on tokenized limit order book (LOB) message streams. The model learns internal representations of market microstructure and dynamics, particularly focusing on order-flow imbalance, traded volume, and volatility. The study demonstrates that these representations are decodable and causally steerable, suggesting the emergence of a world model.
data_sources: The model is trained on the tokenized message streams of limit order books from eight large-cap US equities.
alpha_potential: The model's ability to decode order-flow imbalance (R^2 ≈ 0.59) and generalize across unseen stocks and metrics (traded volume, volatility) suggests strong potential for generating short-horizon alpha. The causal steerability of the model's state indicates practical applicability in algorithmic trading strategies.
title_cn: 理解用于限价订单簿的state-space基础模型的内部工作机制
summary_cn: 本研究采用8.2M参数的Mamba-3 state-space模型，通过自回归训练学习限价订单簿消息流的内部表示。模型能有效解码订单流不平衡(R^2≈0.59)，并在未知股票和波动率等指标上展现泛化能力。其状态可因果调控的特性为短线算法交易策略提供了实际应用潜力。

title: Lineage-Aware Search Control for LLM-Based Evolutionary Factor Mining
summary: Formulaic alpha factor mining searches for symbolic expressions that transform market data into predictive signals. Recent LLM-based evolutionary factor mining methods use large language models as semantic variation operators. Under the conventional LLM-EA paradigm, stochastic variation and fitness-based selection can leave the search weakly directed and concentrated around a narrow set of structurally similar factors. We argue that these limitations arise because current methods mainly organize search at the individual and population levels, leaving lineage-level control underused. A lineage connects successive factor variants through evolutionary descent. We propose LineageEvo, which uses lineage in two coupled forms of search control: (1) lineage-conditioned LLM variation, which distills Lineage-Scoped Search Experience into operator-specific priors and fuses them with global operator priors, providing persistent, lineage-relevant guidance for LLM generation; and (2) lineage-stratified search allocation, which balances factor quality against lineage concentration by distributing the search budget across lineages during evolutionary search. Together, these mechanisms make semantic variation more direction aware and prevent branches from dominating the evolution, thereby promoting the discovery of predictive and diverse factors. We evaluate LineageEvo on CSI 500 and S&P 500 in terms of factor predictiveness, portfolio performance, search efficiency, and lineage- and expression-level diversity. LineageEvo achieves the strongest predictive performance on both markets, while LSPS produces a more balanced lineage distribution and a structurally broader factor pool. The results support lineage as a useful intermediate unit for controlling LLM-based evolutionary factor search.
core_methodology: LineageEvo combines lineage-conditioned LLM variation and lineage-stratified search allocation to enhance evolutionary factor mining. The method uses lineage-level control to guide LLM-based semantic variation, ensuring persistent relevance and preventing structural dominance in the factor pool.
data_sources: CSI 500 and S&P 500 market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology promotes the discovery of diverse and predictive factors by balancing lineage concentration and search allocation, potentially uncovering novel alpha signals not captured by conventional factor mining approaches.
title_cn: 基于LLM的进化因子挖掘的谱系感知搜索控制
summary_cn: 该研究提出LineageEvo方法，通过谱系条件化的LLM变异和谱系分层搜索分配，优化了进化因子挖掘过程。在CSI 500和S&P 500上的实验表明，该方法能发现更多样化和预测性更强的因子，为量化投资提供了新的因子挖掘途径。

title: Combinatorial Arbitrage in Prediction Markets
summary: We develop a framework to identify and quantify arbitrage across logically related prediction-market contracts. We prove that prices outside the convex hull of admissible payoff vectors admit arbitrage and identify optimal arbitrage portfolios through integer programming. Using venue metadata and semantic analysis of resolution criteria, we recover 1.9 million logical relations and compile them into constraint systems covering more than 255,000 contracts. We replay full-depth Polymarket order books to simulate an arbitrageur executing these portfolios against resting orders. Among settled portfolios, an ideal arbitrageur that takes the full displayed depth of every opportunity and reuses its capital at resolution earns a risk-free return of 3.5% a week after spreads and fees. We find that arbitrage opportunities persist longer and attract less observed participation where relation discovery and execution are more costly.
core_methodology: The paper develops a framework for identifying arbitrage opportunities in prediction markets through integer programming and convex hull analysis of admissible payoff vectors. It uses semantic analysis and venue metadata to establish logical relations between contracts.
data_sources: Polymarket order books (prediction market data), venue metadata, and resolution criteria from prediction markets.
alpha_potential: Exploits pricing inefficiencies in logically related prediction-market contracts, showing potential for 3.5% weekly risk-free returns after accounting for spreads and fees. Identifies persistent arbitrage opportunities where relation discovery is costly.
title_cn: 预测市场中的组合套利
summary_cn: 本研究开发了一个系统框架来识别和量化预测市场中逻辑相关合约的套利机会。通过整数规划和凸包分析，论文证明了可获取3.5%周化无风险收益的可行性（扣除点差和费用后）。该方法对发现成本较高的套利机会尤其有效，显示出在预测市场中持续套利的潜力。

title: A Model-Free Continuous-Time RL Algorithm from Discrete-Time Off-Policy Data with End-to-End Guarantees
summary: In this paper, we study continuous-time reinforcement learning, where the state follows an unknown stochastic differential equation but only a fixed off-policy batch of discrete-time transitions is available. Standard discrete-time Q-learning becomes problematic as the sampling interval shrinks, because differences between action values vanish. Continuous-time alternatives, such as Deep Advantage Updating and martingale q-learning, preserve the action signal but jointly learn a value function and an action-dependent critic. Building on the PhiBE-Q formulation (arXiv:2606.21925), we develop a model-free PhiBE policy iteration (PhiBE-PI) framework that uses a single state-action critic while preserving the continuous-time action-ranking scale. At each iteration, the framework learns the critic directly from sampled increments and uses it to improve the policy. The same batch is reused throughout, without explicitly estimating the drift or diffusion. We further develop an implementation under linear function approximation and establish a local end-to-end suboptimality guarantee for the learned policy. Our analysis quantifies how errors from time discretization, function approximation, and finite-sample policy evaluation propagate through policy iteration. It accounts for the dependence of successive policies on the reused data, so the guarantee does not require a fresh batch at each iteration. Moreover, we identify a bias-variance trade-off: smaller sampling intervals improve the approximation to the continuous-time problem but can increase statistical error at a fixed sample size. Thus, finer time discretization does not necessarily lead to better policy performance.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a model-free continuous-time reinforcement learning algorithm (PhiBE-PI) that adapts discrete-time off-policy data for continuous-time environments. It addresses the vanishing action signal issue in Q-learning as sampling intervals shrink by learning a single state-action critic directly from sampled increments, enabling policy improvement without explicit drift or diffusion estimation.
data_sources: The algorithm utilizes a fixed off-policy batch of discrete-time state transitions, which in financial contexts could be derived from historical market data, order book snapshots, or trade executions.
alpha_potential: This approach could be valuable for high-frequency trading (HFT) and algorithmic execution strategies where precise timing and continuous-time decision-making are crucial. The bias-variance trade-off identified (finer discretization vs. statistical error) is particularly relevant for optimizing sampling intervals in market microstructure applications.
title_cn: 基于离散时间离策略数据的免模型连续时间强化学习算法及端到端保证
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种免模型的连续时间强化学习算法(PhiBE-PI)，可将离散时间的离策略数据直接应用于连续时间环境，解决了传统Q学习在时间间隔缩小时动作信号消失的问题。这种技术特别适用于高频交易场景，通过优化采样间隔来平衡连续时间近似与统计误差，为算法执行和市微观结构策略提供了新的方法论。

title: Truncated Out-of-Bag Probability Gain: A Noise-Robust Criterion for Random-Forest Wrapper Feature Selection
summary: Random-Forest wrapper feature selection can use out-of-bag (OOB) predictions as a built-in validation signal, but the criteria that decide each forward step accumulate OOB estimation noise. We propose TOP-Gain (Truncated Out-of-bag Probability Gain), which scores a candidate feature by the mean sample-level increase in the OOB probability of the true class, with decreases truncated at zero. Under a simple noise model, truncation removes about two-thirds of the noise variance contributed by unaffected samples while preserving the signal, and it makes the ranking of candidate features markedly more reproducible. In a pre-registered benchmark on 26 OpenML-CC18 datasets, TOP-Gain achieved the best mean rank in area under the ROC curve (ROC-AUC), accuracy and Macro-F1 among 15 methods; it was significantly better than 13 of 14 baselines and matched the accuracy of VSURF with 21 times less single-core computation. Within an identical wrapper, it selected significantly more stable feature sets than net-gain, Brier, log-loss and accuracy criteria without loss of accuracy. A confirmatory study on 24 further datasets replicated the advantage over all baselines. The accuracy gains were broad rather than tied to specific dataset characteristics, and, as pre-registered, the stability gain grew as relevant features became sparser
core_methodology: The paper introduces TOP-Gain (Truncated Out-of-bag Probability Gain), a noise-robust criterion for Random-Forest wrapper feature selection. It uses truncated OOB probability gain to reduce noise variance while preserving signal, resulting in more stable feature sets without loss of accuracy.
data_sources: The study is evaluated across 26 OpenML-CC18 datasets and later confirmed on 24 additional datasets, demonstrating broad applicability without requiring financial market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology enhances feature selection stability and accuracy, which can improve signal extraction in trading strategies by identifying more robust features with computational efficiency (21 times faster than VSURF).
title_cn: 截断袋外概率增益：一种噪声鲁棒的随机森林包装器特征选择准则
summary_cn: 本研究提出TOP-Gain方法，通过截断袋外概率增益实现噪声鲁棒的随机森林特征选择。在26个数据集上的预注册基准测试中，其在ROC-AUC、准确率和Macro-F1指标上表现最佳，且计算效率显著高于基准方法21倍。该方法能稳定选择特征集而不损失精度，适用于高频交易中快速准确的特征筛选。

title: CrashGym: Measuring the Decision Value of Experimentation for LLM Agents in Counterfactual Market Crashes
summary: Language-model agents are increasingly asked to run experiments, yet benchmarks rarely measure whether those experiments improve the decisions they are meant to inform. We introduce CrashGym, a deterministic, replayable limit-order-book simulator in which an agent must choose between a deleveraging intervention and a liquidity backstop for a market about to suffer a shock-triggered crash. Before committing, the agent may query intervention experiments in a laboratory realization of the market. Its choice is then scored on an independently seeded target realization in which the simulator executes every feasible intervention, so regret relative to the best intervention is computed by directly simulating every alternative on the same target repeats, with no human or model-based judging. The simulator implements each amplification channel---persistent price impact, liquidity withdrawal, margin-driven liquidation, and an evolving strategy mix---as an explicit mechanism that can be switched on in stages. In a prospectively specified study on 24 newly sampled worlds, laboratory access reduces the mean regret of the one deployment with a complete record (Luna) from 8.878 to 3.785, a paired reduction of 5.092 utility units (nominal 95% world-bootstrap interval: 1.028--9.507), or 57.4% of the OBSERVE-ONLY mean. Prospective comparisons for two further deployments are incomplete; in a separate exploratory study, mean regret is lower with laboratory access for all four deployments evaluated. A laboratory whose strategy mix evolves endogenously yields no established advantage over one with a fixed mix. CrashGym thus measures the value of experimentation as avoided decision loss and lets simulator detail be judged by the decisions it supports.
core_methodology: Deterministic, replayable limit-order-book simulator for evaluating LLM agent decisions in market crash scenarios, with explicit mechanisms for various market amplification channels (price impact, liquidity withdrawal, margin liquidation, strategy mix evolution)
data_sources: Simulated limit order book data with configurable market conditions and crash scenarios
alpha_potential: Potential to develop crash-resilient strategies by quantifying the value of pre-crash experimentation and intervention effectiveness in synthetic but realistic market conditions
title_cn: CrashGym: 测量大语言模型代理在反事实市场崩盘中的实验决策价值
summary_cn: CrashGym开发了一个可重放的限价订单簿模拟器，用于量化LLM代理在市场崩溃情景下的实验价值。通过明确模拟价格影响、流动性撤出等市场机制，可评估不同干预策略在合成市场中的效果，为开发抗崩溃交易策略提供依据。初步研究显示实验访问能显著降低决策损失。

title: Design and Tuning of Multi-Agent Systems Using Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization
summary: Designing effective multi-agent systems (MAS) remains a challenging and resource-intensive task. We propose a Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework for automatically discovering task-specific MAS topologies. The approach combines evolutionary operators to generate diverse workflow graphs with Bayesian optimization to focus cost intensive evaluations on promising candidates. In contrast to LLM-based candidate selection, our approach uses a graph-aware Gaussian Process and Expected Improvement to provide an explicit selection criterion during evolutionary search. We evaluate the method on BigCodeBench for code generation and on a tabular preprocessing benchmark using TabPFN. On BigCodeBench, evolved architectures achieve the highest overall performance among the evaluated agent systems. On temporal tabular datasets, optimized MAS preprocessing improves over the default TabPFN model on several tasks, while remaining competitive on IID datasets. Overall, the results demonstrate the potential of Bayesian selection for guiding evolutionary MAS search under expensive evaluation budgets.
core_methodology: Bayesian Evolutionary Optimization framework combining evolutionary operators with Bayesian optimization to automatically discover optimal multi-agent system (MAS) topologies, using graph-aware Gaussian Process for selection criteria.
data_sources: Evaluated on BigCodeBench for code generation and temporal tabular datasets (implicitly suggesting potential application to structured financial data).
alpha_potential: Method could optimize trading agent workflows (e.g., multi-instrument execution systems) or feature preprocessing pipelines for financial models, particularly where evaluation costs are high (e.g., backtesting complex strategies). Bayesian optimization could efficiently search strategy parameter spaces.
title_cn: 基于贝叶斯进化优化的多智能体系统设计与调优
summary_cn: 本研究提出一种贝叶斯进化优化框架，可自动发现任务最优的多智能体系统拓扑结构。该方法结合进化算法生成多样化工作流，并通过贝叶斯优化聚焦高潜候选方案，对量化交易中复杂的多策略协同优化、高频交易系统参数调优具有应用潜力。

title: Leveraging Time-Series Foundation Models for Financial Crime Detection
summary: Financial crime detection requires identifying illicit activity within large transaction networks, where suspicious behaviour is rare and unfolds over time. Existing graph-based methods capture relationships among accounts but typically underuse the temporal behaviour encoded in account transaction histories. We introduce Temporal-Context Edge Enrichment (TCEE), a framework that addresses this gap by summarising each account's transaction history with a frozen time-series foundation model (TSFM), and enriching each transaction's representation with the relevant temporal context from these summaries. These enriched representations can be scored directly for edge classification, or fed into a graph neural network (GNN) as edge features to capture broader structural information. Across six AMLWorld datasets, TCEE improves PR-AUC over the strongest evaluated baseline on five by a relative 10.8% on average, while training 6.0x faster end-to-end. Feeding TCEE's representations into a GNN raises PR-AUC a further 4.8% on the four smaller datasets. On an Ethereum phishing dataset, we show that TSFM-generated account representations fed into a GNN are also effective for node classification, improving PR-AUC by 14.5% over the strongest baseline. As TSFMs continue to advance, our results suggest they can strengthen financial crime detection by capturing temporal signals that complement graph-based approaches.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Temporal-Context Edge Enrichment (TCEE), a framework that leverages time-series foundation models (TSFMs) to summarize account transaction histories and enrich transaction representations. These representations can be used directly for edge classification or fed into a Graph Neural Network (GNN) for capturing structural information.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on six AMLWorld datasets and an Ethereum phishing dataset, focusing on transaction histories and network structures.
alpha_potential: The approach improves financial crime detection by capturing temporal signals in transaction data that complement graph-based methods, potentially aiding in identifying anomalous trading patterns or manipulative behaviors in markets.
title_cn: 利用时间序列基础模型进行金融犯罪检测
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种时间上下文边增强（TCEE）框架，结合时间序列基础模型和GNN来提升金融犯罪检测能力。该方法通过捕捉交易历史中的时间信号和结构信息，为量化异常交易行为提供了新思路，对识别市场操纵等行为有潜在应用价值。

title: SCDM: Scalable Causal Discovery in Nonlinear Temporal Systems with Meta-Learning
summary: Causal discovery from nonlinear multivariate time series is challenging in high-dimensional systems, where the number of candidate directed relations grows quadratically with the number of variables. Existing methods are often limited by target-wise model fitting, repeated conditional testing, or expensive graph-search procedures. We propose SCDM, a shared-parameter meta-learning framework for scalable temporal causal discovery. SCDM treats each target variable as a task while learning a shared temporal predictor and a shared causal-strength matrix across tasks. Each meta-episode updates only a subset of target-variable tasks, allowing the model to accumulate structural evidence across the full system without exhaustive target-wise optimization. After training, a post-training graph readout converts the learned predictor into continuous directed causal scores for threshold-independent evaluation. We also provide a finite-error recovery principle showing that, under fully observed delayed-system assumptions and a positive risk-gap condition, thresholding SCDM scores recovers the graph when statistical, meta-optimization, and readout errors are below the population margin. Experiments on controlled synthetic, neuroimaging-inspired, high-dimensional, and real-world temporal benchmarks demonstrate competitive causal recovery and improved scalability in large temporal systems.
core_methodology: Shared-parameter meta-learning framework for scalable temporal causal discovery in high-dimensional nonlinear systems. Learns a shared temporal predictor and causal-strength matrix across tasks (variables), with partial updates per meta-episode for efficiency. Post-training graph readout converts learned predictors into causal scores.
data_sources: Applicable to any multivariate financial time series (e.g., asset prices, order book features, macroeconomic indicators). Paper tests on synthetic, neuroimaging-inspired, and real-world temporal benchmarks (likely transferable to market data).
alpha_potential: Enables discovery of latent causal structures in market regimes - valuable for: (1) Momentum/contrarian strategy timing by identifying lead-lag relationships, (2) Risk factor decomposition in portfolio optimization, (3) Market microstructure analysis via causal order flow graphs.
title_cn: SCDM：基于元学习的非线性时序系统可扩展因果发现方法
summary_cn: SCDM提出一种元学习框架，通过共享参数结构和分批次任务更新，高效发现高维非线性时序数据中的因果结构。该技术可应用于市场多变量分析，揭示资产价格间的领先滞后关系、风险传导路径等，为动量策略择时、组合风险分解提供新方法论。

title: Quant-Arena: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Quantitative Trading Research
summary: Quantitative research is an iterative loop: a researcher proposes a market hypothesis, implements it as an executable signal, tests it on historical data, and decides what to keep. Existing benchmarks score formulas, code, or individual trading decisions, leaving open whether large language models (LLMs) can complete this loop and produce strategies that work beyond the research period. We introduce Quant-Arena, a benchmark and public leaderboard for end-to-end quantitative research on real A-share market data. A model constructs features and stock-scoring code, receives feedback only on 2022--2023, and freezes one strategy for assessment on the sealed year 2024. A cash-account evaluator applies trading constraints and costs, including market impact estimated from a simulated order book. Scores are dominated by realized excess return and complemented by signal quality and the diversity of features used by the strategy. We evaluate nine frontier models, among which GPT-6 Astra scores highest; yet no model beats the equal-weight market in 2024. Quant-Arena is open to submissions from any model or agent harness.
core_methodology: Large Language Models (LLMs) are employed to construct features and stock-scoring code, with trading strategies evaluated on historical data and tested on a sealed year to ensure robustness.
data_sources: Real A-share market data from 2022-2023 for training, with 2024 as the sealed test year to evaluate strategy performance.
alpha_potential: LLMs may generate unique features and strategies not commonly used by human traders. The benchmark evaluates excess returns, signal quality, and feature diversity, potentially uncovering market inefficiencies.
title_cn: Quant-Arena：量化交易研究中大语言模型代理的基准测试
summary_cn: Quant-Arena 是一个针对A股市场的端到端量化研究基准，用于评估大语言模型（LLMs）在特征构建、选股策略方面的能力。模型使用2022-2023年数据进行训练，并在2024年冻结策略进行测试，通过超额收益、信号质量和特征多样性来评估策略的实际交易价值。当前评测中，GPT-6 Astra得分最高，但仍未跑赢等权市场。该平台开放任何模型或代理的提交。

title: Energy-Based Transfer for Reinforcement Learning
summary: Reinforcement learning remains sample inefficient, particularly when agents must adapt over time to related but distinct tasks, as in continual learning settings. Efficiency can be improved by transferring knowledge from a pretrained teacher policy to guide exploration in new but related tasks. However, if the new task sufficiently differs from the teacher's training task, the transferred guidance may be sub-optimal and bias exploration toward low-reward behaviors. We propose an energy-based transfer learning method that uses out-of-distribution detection to selectively issue guidance, enabling the teacher to intervene only in states within its training distribution. We theoretically link energy scores to state-visitation patterns under on-policy reinforcement learning. Empirically, our method improves sample efficiency and performance across both single-task and multi-task settings.
core_methodology: Energy-based transfer learning for reinforcement learning, using out-of-distribution detection to selectively apply teacher policy guidance to improve exploration efficiency in new but related tasks.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned in the abstract, but applicable to financial time series data, order book data, or other market microstructure data where reinforcement learning is used.
alpha_potential: The method could improve the efficiency of reinforcement learning-based trading strategies by better leveraging prior knowledge (e.g., from similar instruments or market regimes) while avoiding negative transfer when market conditions change significantly. This adaptive knowledge transfer could help capture regime shifts or exploit recurring patterns more efficiently.
title_cn: 基于能量的强化学习迁移方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种基于能量模型的强化学习迁移方法，通过异常检测选择性地应用教师策略指导。对于量化交易，这能提高策略在新市场环境下的适应效率，避免负迁移，适用于跨品种策略迁移或市场状态变化的场景。

title: Structured Temporal Causality for Interpretable Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Real-world multivariate time series anomalies are rare and often unlabeled. Additionally, prevailing methods rely on increasingly complex architectures tuned to benchmarks, detecting only fragments of anomalous segments and overstating performance. In this paper, we introduce OracleAD, a simple and interpretable unsupervised framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection. OracleAD encodes each variable's past sequence into a single causal embedding to jointly predict the present time point and reconstruct the input window, effectively modeling temporal dynamics. These embeddings then undergo a self-attention mechanism to project them into a shared latent space and capture spatial relationships. These relationships are not static, since they are modeled by a property that emerges from each variable's temporal dynamics. The projected embeddings are aligned to a Stable Latent Structure (SLS) representing normal-state relationships. Anomalies are identified using a dual scoring mechanism based on prediction error and deviation from the SLS, enabling fine-grained anomaly diagnosis at each time point and across individual variables. Since any noticeable SLS deviation originates from embeddings that violate the learned temporal causality of normal data, OracleAD directly pinpoints the root-cause variables at the embedding level. OracleAD achieves state-of-the-art results across multiple real-world datasets and evaluation protocols, while remaining interpretable through SLS.
core_methodology: OracleAD is an unsupervised framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection that models temporal causality and spatial relationships through causal embeddings and a self-attention mechanism. It identifies anomalies by deviations from a Stable Latent Structure (SLS) and uses a dual scoring mechanism for precise anomaly diagnosis.
data_sources: The method is designed for multivariate time series data and is evaluated on real-world datasets. Given the abstract mentions real-world datasets, it's inferred to be applicable to financial time series data (e.g., stock prices, trading volumes).
alpha_potential: The ability to detect anomalies in financial time series and identify root-cause variables can be leveraged for real-time risk management, algorithmic trading, and arbitrage by detecting unusual market behaviors before they become widely recognized.
title_cn: 基于结构化时序因果关系的可解释多元时间序列异常检测
summary_cn: OracleAD通过因果嵌入和自注意力机制，建模变量间的时序因果关系和空间关系，检测多元时间序列中的异常。其稳定的潜在结构（SLS）和双重评分机制实现了高精度的异常诊断与根因定位，在金融时间序列（如价格、交易量）分析中，可用于实时风险管理与算法交易，检测市场异常行为，捕捉潜在Alpha机会。

title: Accurate and Efficient Multi-Channel Time Series Forecasting via Sparse Attention Mechanism
summary: The task of multi-channel time series forecasting is ubiquitous in numerous fields such as finance, supply chain management, and energy planning. It is critical to effectively capture complex dynamic dependencies within and between channels for accurate predictions. However, traditional method paid few attentions on learning the interaction among channels. This paper proposes Linear-Network (Li-Net), a novel architecture designed for multi-channel time series forecasting that captures the linear and non-linear dependencies among channels. Li-Net dynamically compresses representations across sequence and channel dimensions, processes the information through a configurable non-linear module and subsequently reconstructs the forecasts. Moreover, Li-Net integrates a sparse Top-K Softmax attention mechanism within a multi-scale projection framework to address these challenges. A core innovation is its ability to seamlessly incorporate and fuse multi-modal embeddings, guiding the sparse attention process to focus on the most informative time steps and feature channels. Through the experiment results on multiple real-world benchmark datasets demonstrate that Li-Net achieves competitive performance compared to state-of-the-art baseline methods. Furthermore, Li-Net provides a superior balance between prediction accuracy and computational burden, exhibiting significantly lower memory usage and faster inference times. Detailed ablation studies and parameter sensitivity analyses validate the effectiveness of each key component in our proposed architecture. Keywords: Multivariate Time Series Forecasting, Sparse Attention Mechanism, Multimodal Information Fusion, Non-linear relationship
core_methodology: Li-Net integrates a sparse Top-K Softmax attention mechanism within a multi-scale projection framework to capture both linear and non-linear dependencies among channels in multi-channel time series data. It dynamically compresses representations across sequence and channel dimensions, processes information through a configurable non-linear module, and reconstructs forecasts.
data_sources: Multiple real-world benchmark datasets (likely including financial time series data given the finance mention in the abstract). Specific datasets not named in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to effectively capture complex dynamic dependencies within and between channels could uncover predictive signals in multivariate financial time series (e.g., cross-asset relationships, factor interactions). The sparse attention mechanism may help identify the most informative time steps and feature channels for trading signals.
title_cn: 基于稀疏注意力机制的精准高效多通道时间序列预测
summary_cn: 本文提出的Li-Net架构通过稀疏Top-K Softmax注意力机制和多尺度投影框架，有效捕捉多通道时序数据（如跨资产价格序列）中的线性/非线性依赖关系，在预测精度与计算效率间取得平衡，对开发基于多变量市场数据的量化策略具有实用价值。

title: Path-Coupled Bellman Flows for Distributional Reinforcement Learning
summary: Distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) models the full return distribution, but existing finite-support or quantile-based methods rely on projections, while recent flow-based approaches can suffer from \emph{boundary mismatch} at the flow source or from \emph{high-variance} bootstrapping when current and successor noises are independent. We propose Path-Coupled Bellman Flows (PCBF), a continuous-time DRL method that learns return distributions with flow matching using \textbf{source-consistent Bellman-coupled paths}: the current path starts from the required base prior at $t{=}0$, reaches the Bellman target at $t{=}1$, and maintains a pathwise affine relation to the successor flow at intermediate times (without requiring time-$t$ marginals to satisfy a distributional Bellman fixed point for all $t$). PCBF couples current and successor return flows through shared base noise and uses a $\lambda$-parameterized control-variate target: $\lambda{=}0$ recovers an unbiased sample Bellman target, while $\lambda{>}0$ trades controlled bias for variance reduction. Experiments on analytically tractable MRPs, OGBench, and D4RL show improved distributional fidelity and training stability, and competitive offline RL performance.
core_methodology: Continuous-time distributional reinforcement learning (DRL) method that learns return distributions with flow matching using source-consistent Bellman-coupled paths. The approach couples current and successor return flows through shared base noise and uses a λ-parameterized control-variate target for variance reduction.
data_sources: Primarily tested on analytically tractable MRPs, OGBench, and D4RL datasets. In finance, could be applied to returns data from equities, FX, or futures markets.
alpha_potential: Improved modeling of full return distributions could lead to better risk-adjusted trading strategies by capturing tail behaviors more accurately. The variance control mechanism may improve stability in strategy backtesting and live trading environments.
title_cn: 分布强化学习中的路径耦合贝尔曼流方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出了PCBF方法，通过基于连续时间的路径耦合贝尔曼流来更精确地建模回报分布。在量化交易中，该方法可以改善对市场极端事件概率分布的建模，优化风险管理策略，并通过λ参数实现方差控制，提升策略回测稳定性。

title: Beyond Accuracy: Measuring Logical Compliance of Predictive Models
summary: Machine learning models are predominantly evaluated through predictive performance metrics such as ranking quality, prediction error, or classification accuracy. While these metrics effectively quantify how closely predictions match the ground truth, they do not assess whether model outputs respect predefined logical or domain-specific constraints. In high-stakes applications, including healthcare, finance, and autonomous systems, logical consistency can be as critical as predictive accuracy, yet no standard metric captures this dimension. We introduce the Rule Violation Score (RVS), a complementary evaluation metric that quantifies the extent to which a predictive model respects a given set of logical rules, independently of predictive accuracy. RVS treats hard rules (strict constraints) and soft rules (statistical regularities) differently, can be evaluated on any dataset and on any predictive model expressed over a relational vocabulary, and can be computed using SQL queries that are automatically generated for Horn rules. Beyond evaluating models, RVS can also evaluate the logical consistency of training datasets and help identify poorly defined rules. We evaluate RVS on three benchmarks covering knowledge graph link prediction and relational regression, including rule-based, embedding-based, and neuro-symbolic predictive models. Our results demonstrate that two models achieving comparable predictive accuracy can exhibit substantially different levels of logical compliance, revealing differences in model behavior that standard metrics fail to capture.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Rule Violation Score (RVS), a metric designed to evaluate the logical compliance of predictive models with predefined constraints. It differentiates between hard and soft rules and can be computed using SQL queries for Horn rules.
data_sources: The methodology can be applied to any dataset and any predictive model expressed over a relational vocabulary, making it versatile for financial datasets including market data, transaction records, and relational financial databases.
alpha_potential: In quant finance, ensuring models comply with logical constraints (e.g., no arbitrage conditions, accounting identities) can reduce erroneous predictions and improve strategy robustness. RVS can help identify models that, while accurate, violate critical financial rules, thus uncovering hidden risks.
title_cn: 超越准确性：预测模型的逻辑合规性测量
summary_cn: 本文提出的规则违反分数（RVS）可用于评估预测模型是否遵守预定义的逻辑或领域特定约束。在量化交易中，RVS有助于确保模型不仅预测准确，还符合关键金融规则（如无套利条件），从而提高策略的稳健性和风险管理能力。

title: HybridResearcher: Bridging the Structured-Unstructured Boundary for Deep Research Agents
summary: While LLM agents are increasingly capable of gathering and synthesizing evidence from a single homogeneous source, such as structured tables or unstructured data, real-world analytical questions frequently span heterogeneous sources. For example, answering one enterprise question may require both a result computed over an internal database and evidence found on the web. Recent evaluations on benchmarks like HybridDeepResearch show that even frontier agents struggle when evidence must cross this boundary. While these benchmarks have exposed the limitation, methodologies to explicitly teach cross-source reasoning remain absent. To address this, we introduce HybridResearcher, a 4B agent trained to bridge evidence across the structured and unstructured boundary. To build it, we synthesize cross-source bridge trajectories by starting with validated single-source tasks-such as existing text-to-SQL or web search queries-and fabricating the missing source around a bridge entity drawn from the seed's own output. We retain a sample only when strict construction gates confirm that neither side alone suffices, ensuring the data requires true cross-source interdependence. Finally, we train on this curated dataset using supervised fine-tuning followed by reinforcement learning. Evaluated on the existing HybridDeepResearch benchmark, HybridResearcher improves over our base model, Qwen3.5-4B, by 30.0 points pass@8 and surpasses the far larger Qwen3.5-397B-A17B by 8.3 points, while also improving over its base model on established, held-out single-source benchmarks (BrowseComp and BrowseComp-Plus), demonstrating that this complex cross-source reasoning can be taught directly to small models without triggering catastrophic forgetting.
core_methodology: HybridResearcher employs supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning to teach cross-source reasoning between structured (e.g., databases) and unstructured (e.g., web) data sources, creating an agent capable of synthesizing information from heterogeneous sources.
data_sources: Structured (e.g., internal databases, financial tables) and unstructured (e.g., web search results, news articles) data sources.
alpha_potential: Potential for uncovering complex signals by combining structured financial data (e.g., market data, fundamentals) with unstructured data (e.g., news, social media sentiment, alternative data), enabling more nuanced trading strategies that leverage cross-source insights.
title_cn: HybridResearcher：跨越结构化与非结构化边界的深度研究智能体
summary_cn: HybridResearcher通过监督微调和强化学习训练一个4B参数的智能体，使其能够在结构化（如数据库）和非结构化（如网络）数据源之间进行跨源推理。该技术在金融交易中具有潜在应用价值，可通过结合市场数据和新闻/社交媒体等非结构化数据，识别更复杂的交易信号。

title: S$^2$-MAS: A Society-Scale Multi-Agent Simulation Framework with 500 Million Household Persona Agents
summary: Simulating economic responses at society scale requires agents whose decisions reflect household circumstances and the effects of earlier actions. We introduce S$^2$-MAS, a society-scale multi-agent simulation framework built on 500 million synthetic household personas grounded in real-survey data. Its Genese engine separates decisions from state updates, while reusable financial scenarios and application ledgers track consumption, cash, debt and payments. Sharp-421m-mlx, a compact decision model trained with SFT + RLCD on 2.93 million examples, achieves 74.55% accuracy and 38.37% question-macro F1 in consumer financial-choice scenarios, outperforming Jev 1.13 and GLM-5.3-Flash on both measures. We evaluate eight financial task families and simulate 12 million distinct household agents in paired purchase-funding conditions. Jointly raising purchase goals and approved credit limits increases consumption, with responses differing across age and income groups. Education, employment and household-size differences persist after age--income standardization and mainly reflect transitions from deferral to purchase. Asset and debt groups differ in cash drawdown, repayment and closing debt. A 24-month panel varies purchase goals under a common credit product, with repayment and arrears updating subsequent offers. S$^2$-MAS links heterogeneous household decisions to evolving consumption, cash and repayment paths, supporting economic experiments across household groups, population scales and time horizons.
core_methodology: A society-scale multi-agent simulation framework (S$^2$-MAS) built on 500 million synthetic household personas, with Sharp-421m-mlx model trained using SFT + RLCD for financial decision-making. The framework enables simulation of heterogeneous household decisions affecting consumption, cash flow, and debt repayment.
data_sources: Real-survey data for generating synthetic household personas and financial scenarios tracking consumption, cash, debt, and payments.
alpha_potential: Potential to uncover macroeconomic trends and consumer behavior patterns that influence market sectors. The framework can simulate responses to financial policies, credit changes, and economic shocks, providing insights for macroeconomic trading strategies and consumer sector investments.
title_cn: S$^2$-MAS：基于5亿家庭角色代理的社会规模多智能体模拟框架
summary_cn: S$^2$-MAS通过5亿个基于真实调查数据的合成家庭角色代理，模拟社会规模的金融决策行为。其Sharp-421m-mlx决策模型在消费金融场景中表现优异，能够追踪消费、现金、债务和还款路径。这一框架可用于宏观经济策略研究，通过模拟不同家庭群体对金融政策的反应，为交易策略提供数据支持。

title: Exploiting Concavity Information in Gaussian Process Contextual Bandit Optimization
summary: The contextual bandit models sequential decision-making problems in which rewards depend on both the chosen action and observed context. In many domains such as medicine, business, and engineering, prior knowledge provides structural information about the reward function that can be exploited to improve optimization efficiency. This paper studies settings where, for each observable context, the conditional mean reward is known to be concave with respect to the action variable. To leverage this structure, we develop a contextual bandit algorithm that conditions a Bayesian Gaussian Process posterior on concavity constraints. We propose a novel reward model that combines a concavity-preserving regression spline basis with a constrained GP posterior, yielding a tractable shape-constrained estimator. Building on this model, we construct a UCB algorithm and establish new posterior concentration inequalities for the constrained posterior, leading to regret guarantees that are never worse than applying standard GP-UCB without concavity information and can be strictly tighter when concavity is informative. Experiments on benchmark problems and a Warfarin dosing test application demonstrate substantial reductions in cumulative regret relative to state-of-the-art baselines.
core_methodology: Contextual bandit algorithm leveraging concavity constraints in Gaussian Process posterior for sequential decision-making with structured reward information
data_sources: Benchmark problems and Warfarin dosing test application
alpha_potential: Improved optimization efficiency in reward functions that exhibit concavity, which could be useful in options pricing and portfolio optimization where convexity/concavity relationships are fundamental
title_cn: 利用高斯过程情境赌博机优化中的凹性信息
summary_cn: 本文开发了一种情境赌博机算法，通过结合凹性约束的高斯过程后验，提升具有凹性结构的奖励函数优化效率。该方法在交易领域的期权定价曲线优化等非线性关系建模中具有应用潜力，可通过结构先验知识获取更优决策性能。

title: Proximal Balancing for Causal Effect Estimation under Unmeasured Confounding
summary: Estimating causal effects from observational data is central to science and policy, but the effects are not identified when confounders are unmeasured. Proximal causal inference addresses this problem with proxies of the unmeasured confounders. However, existing proxy-based approaches either designate proxy roles and solve an inverse problem, which is ill-posed and hard to estimate with high-dimensional proxies, or use a latent-variable model, which assumes that the learned latent variable matches the hidden confounder and leaves bias when it does not. To address these challenges, we introduce proximal balancing. It carries the classical idea of covariate balancing to confounders that are observed only through proxies: it learns a low-dimensional summary of the covariates and proxies that makes the treatment groups comparable, and then adjusts for this summary. It needs no designated proxy roles, inverse problem, or latent model. We give identification theory, finite-sample guarantees, and a practical algorithm, PROBE. We demonstrate the method on low-dimensional, high-dimensional, and image proxies and on real-world data.
core_methodology: Proximal balancing - learns a low-dimensional summary of covariates and proxies to make treatment groups comparable, then adjusts for this summary without requiring designated proxy roles, inverse problems, or latent models.
data_sources: Observational data with potential application to financial markets data where unmeasured confounders exist (e.g., investor sentiment, macroeconomic factors).
alpha_potential: Enables more accurate causal effect estimation in financial scenarios with hidden confounders, potentially improving factor models, event studies, and treatment effect estimation (e.g., policy changes or corporate actions).
title_cn: 用于未测量混杂下因果效应估计的近端平衡方法
summary_cn: 该论文提出的近端平衡方法(PROBE)在没有明确代理变量角色或潜在模型假设下，通过学习协变量和代理变量的低维摘要来平衡处理组，为金融场景中存在潜在混杂因素(如未观测的市场情绪或宏观因素)的因果效应估计提供了新工具，可改进因子模型、事件研究和政策效果评估的准确性。

title: Strategic Index Reconstitution: Differential Games, Closed-Loop Equilibria and Mean-Field Dynamics
summary: We study a continuous-time, multiasset trading game around index reconstitution, in which opportunistic traders have heterogeneous beliefs about the future index constitution and interact through transient cross-asset price impact and instantaneous execution costs. Opportunistic traders build inventory based on their individual beliefs about the future index constitution before a public announcement, adjust their positions to the revealed composition, and unwind them against the indexer's prescribed rebalancing trades at the implementation date when the new index composition takes effect. Under a no-price-manipulation condition, we construct a subgame-perfect Nash equilibrium. Its affine feedback policies are computed from a non-standard matrix Riccati equation and linear ODEs whose number and dimensions are independent of population size. Under mean-field scaling, we construct a mean-field equilibrium and obtain quantitative convergence and approximate-Nash bounds. Numerical illustrations show that greater competition among opportunists dampens price swings around implementation and that opportunistic trading lowers the indexer's implementation shortfall unless price resilience is very low. Holding the average belief fixed, greater belief dispersion can increase gross trading volume without changing net aggregate opportunist holdings or price impact.
core_methodology: Continuous-time multi-asset trading game with differential game theory, Nash equilibrium construction under no-price-manipulation condition, mean-field equilibrium analysis
data_sources: Market microstructure data around index reconstitution events, including order flows, execution costs, and cross-asset price impacts
alpha_potential: Opportunistic trading around index reconstitution events where heterogeneous beliefs about future composition create temporary mispricing opportunities. The paper demonstrates how to exploit these through strategic inventory building and unwinding against indexer's rebalancing flows.
title_cn: 战略性指数重组：微分博弈、闭环均衡与均场动力学
summary_cn: 本研究构建了一个连续时间的多资产指数重组交易博弈模型，量化研究者在指数调整公告前建立头寸并在实施阶段平仓的最优策略。通过微分博弈理论证明了纳什均衡的存在，其线性反馈策略可显著降低指数调整执行缺口。该模型为指数套利策略提供了数学框架，特别适用于管理指数跟踪误差或开发事件驱动型算法。

title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
summary: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.
core_methodology: The paper uses reinforcement learning (RL) to train large language model (LLM) agents in market environments, specifically focusing on pricing and trading behaviors. It introduces an audit method to test enforcement mechanisms in agent collusion scenarios.
data_sources: The study likely uses simulated market environments to train and evaluate the LLM agents, as opposed to real-world market data.
alpha_potential: The research provides insights into how RL-trained agents might collude or compete in markets, which could inform the development of more robust automated trading systems that account for such behaviors. However, the direct application to real-world trading is limited due to the use of simulated environments and theoretical focus on agent behaviors.
title_cn: 谁在监管卡特尔？强化学习在市场中教会LLM代理什么
summary_cn: 本研究通过强化学习训练大型语言模型代理在市场定价和交易中的行为，重点分析了代理间的共谋执行机制。研究发现代理主要学习固定规则或模仿对手行为，而非主动惩罚违规者。该成果对理解自动交易系统中的代理共谋行为有参考价值，但需进一步研究如何应用于实际高频交易环境。

title: Towards Realistic Models of Change: A Causal Perspective on Decision-Making and Dynamical Systems
summary: While statistical learning has made remarkable progress in recent decades, driven by large datasets and data-driven protocols that have transformed scientific practice, it still faces a key limitation: it struggles to generalize beyond the data it has seen, often failing under distribution shift. Causality offers a promising solution: causal models focus on the underlying mechanisms of change rather than surface-level associations, enabling robust reasoning under external interventions. This allows systems not only to learn from data, but also to reason about hypothetical scenarios, adapt to new environments, and inform better decisions. This thesis explores how these approaches can inform each other, in two parts. The first part examines algorithmic recourse, that is, identifying which changes an individual can make to overturn an unfavorable decision. We propose an alternative perspective to the established framework, arguing for a more realistic cost function, a reformulation of the problem in causal terms, and the inclusion of a temporal dimension in policy evaluation. The second part focuses on dynamical systems, extending the notions of causal interventions and effects to discrete and continuous stochastic processes. We show that the equilibria of these processes, and how they change following an intervention, can be linked to Structural Causal Models (SCMs), viewed as compressed representations of the underlying temporal dynamics. We argue for the relevance of such temporal causal models, since in real-world scenarios actions take time to produce their effects. The common goal of both parts is practical: the utility, robustness, and trustworthiness of these models depend critically on their ability to realistically represent the underlying phenomena.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on causal models and structural causal models (SCMs) to understand and predict changes in dynamical systems, including temporal dimensions and realistic cost functions.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology implies potential use with time-series data and dynamical systems relevant to financial markets.
alpha_potential: Causal models could improve robustness under distribution shifts, aiding in the development of trading strategies that adapt to new market conditions and interventions. The temporal aspect is particularly relevant for time-series forecasting in finance.
title_cn: 面向现实变化模型：决策与动力系统的因果视角
summary_cn: 本研究通过因果模型和结构因果模型（SCMs）探讨动态系统中的变化，特别关注时间维度和现实成本函数。对于量化交易，该方法可提升在分布变化下的模型鲁棒性，适用于市场条件变化的策略开发，具有时间序列预测的潜力。

title: RL-IF: Tracking Non-local Training Data Influence for Online Reinforcement Learning
summary: Online reinforcement learning (RL) has achieved significant success in decision-making tasks, but modern online RL remains highly sensitive to the quality of training experience. Understanding the contribution of individual training instances is therefore central to data-centric RL, with applications ranging from experience selection to policy interpretation. Existing data attribution methods for online RL primarily focus on local influence within a single training round, overlooking the non-local data influence across multiple training rounds. In this work, we formalize data attribution in online RL through a trajectory-level leave-one-out quantity, RL-LOO, which measures how one training sample influences a downstream target after subsequent online updates have taken place. We then derive RL-IF, a first-order estimator that propagates data influence through both optimization effects and policy-induced sampling effects, and provide theoretical guarantees on its approximation accuracy under smoothness assumptions. Our analysis further disentangles these two effects and shows both theoretically and empirically that the full RL-IF estimator can often be well approximated using the optimization effect alone. Building on this observation, we develop RINSE, a practical data filtering method for online RL. Experiments on standard control benchmarks and an RLHF-style toxicity-mitigation setting show that RINSE improves training efficiency and final performance over standard PPO and local attribution baselines. These results suggest that RL-IF provides a practical and principled framework for understanding and improving online RL.
core_methodology: The paper introduces RL-IF, a first-order estimator that tracks non-local training data influence in online reinforcement learning by considering both optimization effects and policy-induced sampling effects. It also presents RINSE, a practical data filtering method based on RL-IF.
data_sources: The methodology is tested on standard control benchmarks and an RLHF-style toxicity-mitigation setting, suggesting potential applicability to any domain using online RL, including financial markets.
alpha_potential: The method could potentially improve trading strategy performance by better understanding and filtering training data in online RL settings, leading to more efficient learning and better final policy performance.
title_cn: RL-IF：用于在线强化学习的非局部训练数据影响跟踪
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种新的在线强化学习数据归因方法RL-IF，通过量化单一样本对后续训练样本的非局部影响来提高策略学习效率与最终性能。研究发展的RINSE数据过滤方法对改进交易策略的在线学习过程具有潜在价值。

title: Minimax-Optimal Predictive Flow Matching under Distribution Drift
summary: Flow matching learns a generative velocity field by regression, but under distribution drift a field must be deployed before the current data arrive. We study this predictive problem for a fixed, possibly nonconvex, neural class, with dynamic regret against the best represented field of each round. We propose DyProd-FM, which refits flow matching on dyadic historical prefixes and selects among the fits with a sleeping Prod master. Without knowing any drift budget, it attains regret $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_\omega+1,1+\sqrt{T\Omega}\})$ in the relative velocity risk variation $\Omega$ and $\widetilde{O}(\min\{N_\mu+1,1+T^{1/3}V_\mu^{2/3}\})$ in the target-law variation $V_\mu=\sum_t W_2(\mu_{t+1},\mu_t)$, up to approximation and fitting costs. Matching lower bounds for fixed classes show that both rates are optimal in $T$ and in the budgets up to logarithmic factors. Prior optimal dynamic-regret guarantees rely on a convex decision set with strongly convex or exp-concave losses, whereas our class may be nonconvex and no curvature in its parameters is assumed. The target-law rate rests on a second-order link between the two variations, which the base noise of flow matching provides.
core_methodology: Flow matching with dynamic regret minimization under distribution drift using DyProd-FM, which refits on historical prefixes and selects with a sleeping Prod master
data_sources: Generic time-series data with distribution drift (could be applied to financial time series like asset returns)
alpha_potential: Potential for adaptive generative modeling of non-stationary financial data (e.g., changing market regimes or volatility patterns)
title_cn: 分布漂移下的极小极大最优预测流匹配方法
summary_cn: 本论文提出了DyProd-FM方法，通过动态调整流匹配模型来适应分布漂移。对于高频交易中的非平稳市场环境（如波动率变化或状态切换），该方法可被应用于生成自适应交易策略信号。模型不依赖参数凸性假设的特性使其可能适合复杂的金融市场建模。

title: Dissimilarity-Based Markov Decision Processes for Stabilizing State Distributions
summary: Reinforcement learning for stochastic systems typically optimizes expected cumulative rewards, while reliable and repeatable behavior also depends on how the state distribution evolves over time. Optimizing expected return alone does not guarantee that this distribution converges to a desired target or remains stable. This paper develops a theoretical framework for learning policies that stabilize state distributions. We formulate the problem as a Dissimilarity-based Markov Decision Process (DMDP), in which the policy acts on the current state distribution and the objective measures its dissimilarity to a target distribution. We establish sufficient conditions under which the optimal policy makes the target distribution asymptotically stable. To support policy learning, we introduce a finite-dimensional representation of distributions and show how stability guarantees for its parameter dynamics extend to the underlying state distributions. We further develop certificates for the learned policies, including their deployment using estimated distribution parameters. These results quantify how learning and estimation errors affect the guarantees and identify conditions under which learned policies retain asymptotic stability. For practical implementation, we combine distribution estimates and target-dependent rewards with PPO and SAC. A computable example on a linear system illustrates the proposed theoretical certificates. Furthermore, experiments on a HalfCheetah task demonstrate the benefits of distribution feedback and explicit target matching for regulating the velocity distribution.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a Dissimilarity-based Markov Decision Process (DMDP) framework for learning policies that stabilize state distributions, combining distribution estimates and target-dependent rewards with reinforcement learning algorithms like PPO and SAC.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but implied to involve state distributions and target distributions, potentially applicable to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The method could be adapted to stabilize portfolio state distributions or trading strategy performance distributions, potentially reducing volatility and improving risk-adjusted returns by ensuring the state distribution converges to a desired target.
title_cn: 基于差异性的马尔可夫决策过程用于稳定状态分布
summary_cn: 本文提出了一种基于差异性的马尔可夫决策过程（DMDP）框架，用于学习稳定状态分布的策略。通过结合分布估计和目标依赖奖励，该方法可以应用于金融时间序列数据，稳定交易策略或投资组合的状态分布，从而可能降低波动性并提高风险调整后的收益。

title: Distilling Multi-Teacher Scoring Principles for Unsupervised Time Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Time series anomalies take diverse forms, and individual detectors encode different anomaly scoring principles that rarely cover all anomaly types. Recent unsupervised time-series anomaly detectors provide complementary scoring signals, yet deploying them as an ensemble preserves the inference and maintenance cost of every individual detector. We study whether heterogeneous teacher detectors can be distilled into a single lightweight detector in the unsupervised setting, where no anomaly labels are available to define a shared target. AnoMix addresses this by extracting weak pairwise supervision from the training-set anomaly scores of frozen teachers. It normalizes each teacher score sequence independently and trains the student with CoRank, a multi-teacher ranking-distillation objective that converts teacher score gaps into pairwise supervision through teacher consensus. Across seven benchmark datasets, AnoMix successfully integrates complementary teacher scoring principles into a single deployable model, improving over individual detectors and static score ensembles while using a compact student with under 80k parameters on the benchmark settings. A zero-shot variant further shows that the distilled ranking signal transfers to unseen datasets and can outperform large pretrained time-series foundation models for anomaly detection.
core_methodology: Distills unsupervised anomaly detection scoring principles from multiple teacher models into a single lightweight student model using weak pairwise supervision and ranking-distillation objective.
data_sources: Generic time-series benchmark datasets (not financial-specific). Study mentions 7 benchmark datasets but doesn't specify domain.
alpha_potential: Could potentially be adapted for detecting anomalous price/volume patterns in markets, but would require significant modifications to financial time series and validation with market data. Zero-shot transfer capability suggests possible application across markets.

title: Memory-Centric Continual Learning for AI Agents
summary: Autonomous agents powered by foundation models can reason, plan, and use tools, but their fixed weights and context limits hinder sustained learning from experience over long-term deployment. While external memory systems attempt to bridge this gap, they mostly act as passive retrieval caches, evaluated primarily by whether they can recall stored facts or past interactions. Whether memory can drive genuine continual learning remains an open question. In this paper, we introduce Memory-Centric Continual Learning (MCCL), arguing that memory should be judged by whether it improves future actions, not merely what it retrieves. MCCL has three main parts. First, a three-axis taxonomy organizes memory by where state is stored (substrates), what form it takes (assets), and how it is managed (policies). This defines a two-loop lifecycle that updates memory state in an inner loop while refining management policies in an outer loop based on task feedback. Second, an evaluation protocol measures retention under interference, adaptation to change, and task transfer to isolate genuine behavioral gains from simple context expansion. Third, a memory scaling framework models how agent performance scales with experience, storage capacity, and compute budgets across non-parametric and parametric memory. Together, these components reframe agent memory from passive lookup to continuous learning, offering a principled route toward self-improving autonomous agents.
core_methodology: A three-axis taxonomy organizing memory by storage substrates, asset forms, and management policies, combined with a two-loop lifecycle for memory state updates and policy refinement
data_sources: Not explicitly specified (likely generic agent-environment interaction data applicable to financial markets)
alpha_potential: Potential for adaptive learning systems that improve trading strategy performance through continuous memory updating and policy refinement in changing market conditions

title: Cascading Bandits with Noisy Observations: Algorithms and Regret Bounds
summary: We propose a novel stochastic cascading bandit setup where probing an ordered shortlist of $K$ out of $L$ arms incurs position-dependent costs, and the learner observes only noisy feedback regarding each arm's true output. We identify a sub-class of noise models for which the optimal shortlist can be found by sorting arms according to a per-arm score: such a score exists for both selection and ordering when the channel has no false positives, and for ordering alone (but not selection) when measurements are costless; however in general neither selection nor ordering is separable once noise and cost are both present. For the case where both selection and ordering scores exist, we provide a UCB-based algorithm with $O((L-K)\log T)$ instance-dependent regret over a time horizon $T$, which matches an algorithm-agnostic lower bound (up to constant factors). For the more challenging scenario where scores don't exist, we develop a new algorithmic template, DP-UCB, that embeds optimism directly inside an exact dynamic program, yielding $O\big(LK\log T\big)$ regret. Finally, we validate our theoretical results through extensive numerical evaluations and simulations over both synthetic and real-world datasets.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a UCB-based algorithm and a new algorithmic template called DP-UCB for stochastic cascading bandits with noisy observations. It focuses on optimizing ordered shortlists of arms under position-dependent costs and noisy feedback.
data_sources: The paper uses both synthetic and real-world datasets, though the specific nature of the real-world datasets is not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for trading strategy optimization where selection and ordering of assets under noisy market conditions are critical, such as in portfolio construction or order execution strategies.

title: Generative Modeling via Nonlinear Schr\"odinger Bridges and Branching Diffusions
summary: We propose a new generative modeling framework grounded in forward-backward partial differential equations (PDEs). These equations arise naturally in mean-field game (MFG) theory, and are closely related to nonlinear Schr\"odinger systems. Our main contribution is to reinterpret this connection within the setting of generative modeling and to develop an efficient numerical methodology for its practical implementation. Specifically, we derive and characterize a nonlinear extension of the classical Schr\"odinger bridge problem through a coupled system of PDEs, yielding a model we call SBNL (Schr\"odinger Bridge NonLinear). To compute its solution, we design a simulation algorithm based on branching diffusions and the probabilistic representation of semilinear PDEs. The resulting method is embarrassingly parallel, scalable to high dimensions, and applicable to a broad class of nonlinear interaction functionals. We validate the approach through numerical experiments, including recovery of the classical Schr\"odinger bridge, nonlinear extensions with convex penalties (Gross-Pitaevskii) as well as potential interaction terms, and high-dimensional generative tasks such as image synthesis on the MNIST and FFHQ human face dataset. Furthermore, the same framework embeds score-based generative modeling, diffusion models, and tractable gaussian Schr\"odinger bridges.
core_methodology: Generative modeling framework based on forward-backward partial differential equations (PDEs) and nonlinear Schr"odinger bridge problems. Utilizes branching diffusions and probabilistic representation of semilinear PDEs for numerical implementation.
data_sources: Tested on classical Schr"odinger bridge problems and high-dimensional generative tasks such as image synthesis on MNIST and FFHQ datasets. Potentially applicable to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The framework's ability to model complex distributions and handle nonlinear interactions could be adapted for generating synthetic financial market data, modeling joint distributions of asset returns, or enhancing factor-based strategies through improved generative processes.
title_cn: 基于非线性薛定谔桥和分支扩散的生成建模方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出了一种基于前向-后向偏微分方程（PDE）和薛定谔桥理论的生成建模新框架。该框架采用分支扩散技术和半线性PDE的概率表示方法，擅长高维非线性问题建模。量化金融中可用于市场数据生成、因子相关性建模等任务，为开发新型衍生品定价模型或优化投资组合提供数学工具。

title: Rethinking Agentic Model Orchestration for Time Series Forecasting
summary: Time series foundation models (TSFMs) perform unevenly across forecasting tasks. Recent work uses agentic model orchestration (AMO) to select or combine TSFMs, often outperforming individual forecasters. Yet these gains may reflect stronger or more complementary candidates rather than better orchestration. To disentangle these effects, we introduce FairAMO, a controlled evaluation protocol with frozen candidate forecasts. Experiments on GIFT-Eval show that AMO improves accuracy, but its gains are bounded by the candidate TSFMs. The best orchestrators reduce MASE by less than 6% relative to the best single TSFM across all tasks. These gains depend on complementarity (different candidates excel on different tasks) rather than the number of candidates. Adding members yields diminishing returns, and a redundant member can erase these gains. The value of historical evidence also saturates quickly. A few recent windows capture all gains, and further history adds none. These findings separate system-level forecasting gains from the contribution of orchestration itself.
core_methodology: Agentic model orchestration (AMO) for time series forecasting with frozen candidate forecasts, evaluating complementarity and historical evidence utilization
data_sources: GIFT-Eval dataset (specific details not provided in abstract, presumed to contain multiple time series forecasting tasks)
alpha_potential: Potential marginal gains from optimally combining complementary TS forecasting models, though bounded by base model quality (max ~6% MASE improvement observed)

title: Implicit Feature Reweighting for Label-Free Graph Generalization
summary: Graph-level out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization is critical for deploying graph neural networks in real-world applications where distribution shifts are inevitable. Existing approaches typically require class labels during representation learning to decide which substructures are predictive, limiting their applicability. We propose SCARCE, a label-free representation-learning framework that yields distribution-shift-robust graph representations from an environment partition of the training graphs alone, whether that partition comes from dataset metadata or, when none is available, from clustering a self-supervised embedding. Our method operates in two stages: (1) a variational graph autoencoder is warm-started for graph reconstruction; and (2) an adversarial confusion mechanism forces the encoder to produce representations from which a discriminator cannot distinguish environments, while preserving graph-reconstruction fidelity. We provide theoretical analysis showing that environment confusion contracts environment-discriminative directions in the representation space, which, under regularized downstream classifiers, is equivalent to imposing a stronger directional penalty on environment-associated features. This feature-reweighting mechanism reduces reliance on spurious correlations without erasing information, offering a label-free, continuous relaxation of last-layer reweighting methods. Experiments on a controlled synthetic datasets and the DrugOOD datasets show that SCARCE achieves state-of-the-art OOD generalization among label-free methods, using no class labels during representation learning.
core_methodology: SCARCE is a two-stage, label-free graph representation learning framework that uses a variational graph autoencoder for initial graph reconstruction followed by an adversarial confusion mechanism to produce robust representations against distribution shifts. The method implicitly reweights features through environment confusion without requiring class labels.
data_sources: Graph-structured data, demonstrated on controlled synthetic datasets and the DrugOOD dataset (pharmaceutical application data). Could be adapted to financial graph structures such as inter-market relationships, order book networks, or asset correlation graphs.
alpha_potential: Potential in detecting robust patterns in financial networks that persist under market regime changes, though methodology would need significant adaptation to financial data structures. The label-free aspect is valuable as financial labels are often noisy or unavailable.

title: Fast Bayesian Optimization Through Linear Models
summary: Bayesian optimization (BO) is typically used only for problems where the underlying function is deemed "expensive" (e.g. in time or money), with the speed of the BO algorithm being of little importance. In the real world, however, problems span a continuous range of values, going from cheap to expensive. In this paper, we present BO algorithms through the lens of a speed-performance Pareto frontier: we compare BO against faster algorithms like CMA-ES, and highlight how certain regions of the Pareto frontier are currently empty. As a solution, we propose a new set of fast BO methods that exploit the linear structure in existing BO algorithms, for both continuous and combinatorial inputs (from ~10 to 6000+ dimensions). Our methods achieve performance similar to state-of-the-art BO, while being more than $10^2\times$ to $10^3\times$ faster, opening the field of BO to an entirely new class of problems.
core_methodology: The paper introduces fast Bayesian Optimization (BO) methods that leverage linear structures in existing BO algorithms to achieve significant speed improvements while maintaining performance similar to state-of-the-art BO. It addresses problems across a spectrum from cheap to expensive, making BO applicable to a new class of problems.
data_sources: The paper does not specify particular financial data sources but the methodology is generally applicable to optimization problems in trading strategies, such as portfolio allocation or parameter tuning in algorithmic models.
alpha_potential: The speed improvements in Bayesian Optimization can enhance real-time optimization of trading strategies, such as high-frequency trading models or dynamic portfolio rebalancing, where quick parameter tuning is crucial.

title: Local and Global Recursive Ridge Regression for Online Residual Correction of Frozen Multivariate Forecasters under Label Delay
summary: A frozen multi-horizon forecaster can be corrected online from its own residuals. However, under label delay the target of a block arrives only after the whole horizon has passed, and the corrector's retained state grows with the number of channels. Aiming to combine a small retained state with a large error reduction, we propose DRiC (DCT Ridge Corrector), which fits a ridge regression of the leading discrete cosine transform (DCT) coefficients of the next residual block on those of the frozen forecast and of the latest input block, with sufficient statistics updated recursively. Its local variant, DRiC-L, keeps one such regression per channel; its global variant, DRiC-G, pools all channels into one regression, whose statistics do not depend on the channel count. A guard tracks a running scale of the frozen forecast's residual for each channel; it skips updates on blocks far outside that scale and clips the issued correction. We evaluate on seven datasets (four ETT series, Weather with its missing-value codes filled, Electricity, and Traffic) with DLinear, PatchTST, and iTransformer backbones, against 10 naive, gradient-trained, and closed-form methods. DRiC-L with eight DCT coefficients (DRiC-L8) reduces the mean squared error (MSE) by 14.55% on average over 126 conditions, against 12.98% for ELF, the most accurate comparator, while retaining 15-17 times less state, although ELF is more accurate on Traffic. DRiC-G retains 14.6 kB on the 321-channel Electricity data and 18.9 kB on the 862-channel Traffic data and is the most accurate method at or below its state on both. However, 5 to 7 of the 10 comparators, all with at least 10 times its state, are more accurate there. On the unfilled Weather file, DRiC-L8 without the guard has on average 8.0 times the frozen forecast's MSE, whereas with the guard it reduces the MSE by 7.94%. Code: https://github.com/keiotakmin/dric.
core_methodology: Online residual correction using recursive ridge regression applied to frozen multivariate forecasters, with local and global variants (DRiC-L and DRiC-G) that leverage DCT coefficients for efficient state retention
data_sources: Time-series datasets (ETT series, Weather, Electricity, Traffic)
alpha_potential: Potential to improve forecasting accuracy in quantitative trading strategies through efficient online correction of base models, especially in multi-horizon forecasting scenarios where label delays exist
