title: Improved Training of Strong Stochastic Flow Maps
summary: Stochastic flow maps promise few-step sampling of stochastic differential equations (SDEs) by learning to directly jump between times along the solution path, yet training these models to learn this solution map remains difficult. The primary obstacle is the Brownian path itself: it is an infinite-dimensional object which needs to be passed to the neural network and is nowhere differentiable, which makes the implementation of derivative-based losses that power the state-of-the-art deterministic flow maps just out of reach. We identify two core design principles which address these issues: a) represent the Brownian path with a basis which carries higher-order local information, and b) train with an objective that forces the network to use the full representation of the path, not just the first order. To address this, we leverage the shifted Legendre polynomial expansion with a Wong-Zakai styled objective, unlocking derivative-based losses. Finally, we propose a recipe for fine-tuning large pre-trained flow models into strong stochastic flow maps. We ablate through this design space on several toy problems and use our findings to transform a large flow model into a strong stochastic flow map on ImageNet, achieving roughly a three-fold improvement in FD-DINOv2 over SSFM at four NFE.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a method to improve the training of stochastic flow maps for solving stochastic differential equations (SDEs) using neural networks. It leverages shifted Legendre polynomial expansions and a Wong-Zakai styled objective to handle the non-differentiable nature of Brownian paths, enabling derivative-based losses.
data_sources: The paper uses synthetic datasets on toy problems and applies the method to ImageNet, indicating potential adaptability to financial time series data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted to model financial time series more efficiently, potentially improving the speed and accuracy of pricing models, risk assessments, and algorithmic trading strategies that rely on SDEs.

title: Characterizing Oblivious Common-Reward Multi-Player Bandits: Universal Stationarity, Coordination Traps, and Certified Global Rates
summary: This paper presents a theoretical analysis of the oblivious common-reward multi-player multi-armed bandit (OC-MPMAB), a minimal multi-player bandit model in which multiple players select arms simultaneously and observe only a shared reward. Crucially, the players are fully oblivious: they do not observe the actions of other players and do not even know whether any other players exist. The contributions of this work are threefold. First, we prove that the independent gradient-bandit updates applied by the players jointly form an unbiased stochastic gradient estimator of a hidden product-policy objective. This property then yields a universal finite-time first-order stationarity guarantee for every instance. Second, we show that stationarity cannot, in general, be strengthened to global optimality. To illustrate this, we identify a product-policy trap obstruction that rules out the guarantee of global optimality. Third, we show that global optimality can be recovered under structural assumptions on the reward table. To make global optimality achievable, we introduce finite-table certificates that separately characterize product-gradient dominance and self-bounding stochastic noise. We then establish certificate-conditioned bounds on the product-policy gap and pseudo-regret. Consequently, the standard $O(1/t)$ product-policy gap and $O(\log T)$ pseudo-regret rates hold when the certificates are uniform.
core_methodology: Theoretical analysis of multi-player multi-armed bandits with shared rewards, focusing on gradient-based updates, stationarity guarantees, and global optimality conditions under structural assumptions.
data_sources: Theoretical framework with no explicit data sources, but applicable to environments with shared feedback mechanisms (e.g., market impact scenarios or coordinated trading environments).
alpha_potential: Potential application in scenarios where multiple agents (e.g., traders or algorithms) interact in markets with shared rewards or feedback, such as order execution with market impact awareness or cooperative trading strategies. The analysis of coordination traps and global optimality conditions could inform multi-agent strategy design.

title: Evolving with Open Worlds: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Future Forecasting
summary: Most contemporary artificial intelligence (AI) systems are released with frozen parameters and improve through external updates, whereas an ideal system would keep improving from its own experience, a capacity we call recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet studying RSI requires an environment that is continuously changing, objectively verifiable, and naturally grounded, posing a fundamental challenge for agent evolution. Here we introduce DeepEvolve, a sustainable evolution agent system grounded in future event prediction, in which agents continuously interact with a dynamically evolving environment and improve by internalizing and externalizing the experience gained through these interactions. A living environment synthesizes verifiable tasks, and a recursive-evolution engine turns the reasoning trajectory behind each prediction back into capability: decoupling search from prediction adapts parameter-level evolution to the contamination-prone live environment, while distilling reusable skills lets the agent evolve from the limited live trajectories such an environment affords. On the external FutureX leaderboard, which evaluates predictions against real-world outcomes and is updated weekly, our self-improved forecaster ranked first across all systems over three consecutive weeks, achieving up to a 195% improvement in rating. On our synthesized evaluation, it ranked among the top three across four base LLMs, outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 10.7 Bradley--Terry points. More broadly, these results suggest that a system built for self-improvement is best understood as an agent that co-evolves with a genuinely living, open-ended environment, pointing to a shift in AI from training static models on fixed data toward cultivating agents that grow stronger from their own experience, with such an open world as the indispensable basis of that growth.
core_methodology: The paper introduces DeepEvolve, a system for recursive self-improvement (RSI) through continuous interaction with dynamically evolving environments, focusing on future event prediction. It employs a recursive-evolution engine that decouples search from prediction and distills reusable skills from limited live trajectories.
data_sources: The system is evaluated on the external FutureX leaderboard, which updates weekly with real-world outcomes, and on synthesized evaluation tasks. Real-world outcomes and synthetic tasks are used for validation.
alpha_potential: The system's ability to continuously improve and adapt to new data could be leveraged for predictive modeling in financial markets, particularly for forecasting market movements or event-driven strategies. The RSI capability suggests potential for maintaining edge in evolving market conditions.
title_cn: 与开放世界共同进化：面向未来预测的递归自我改进
summary_cn: 本文提出的DeepEvolve系统通过递归自我改进机制，在动态环境中持续优化未来事件预测能力。这种实时适应和学习的方法在量化交易中有潜在应用，可用于市场动态预测和事件驱动策略开发，提升模型在当前不断变化的市场环境中的适应性和预测精度。

title: Asymmetric On-Policy Distillation Learns In-Context Exploration
summary: Sequential decision-making under partial observability is difficult because agents must explore to infer hidden, task-relevant information before acting effectively. Learning such information-gathering behaviors tabula rasa via online reinforcement learning is sample-inefficient, whereas offline imitation averages expert actions across hidden states and fails to learn exploration. In this work, we propose ASTEROID, a simple and effective student--teacher supervised learning framework that can learn test-time exploration. Although a privileged expert never needs to explore, we demonstrate that a history-conditioned student can learn to do so when trained with on-policy contexts: the student first collects on-policy context under partial observability, and the privileged expert provides action labels conditioned on that context. By distilling expert actions directly conditioned on the student's on-policy history, the student learns to systematically resolve partial observability, i.e., search while uncertain and exploit once the hidden state is revealed. This enables efficient test-time exploration (similar to Bayesian posterior sampling) without incurring the impractical training-data costs of reinforcement learning. Across a diverse range of eleven different environments, including discrete exploration benchmarks, robotic manipulation, navigation, and Procgen environments, ASTEROID achieves ~2x higher returns under fixed exploration budgets, uses ~100x fewer interactions than RL baselines, and outperforms frontier models at exploration. Finally, our method transfers policies trained in simulation to vision-denied real-world robot manipulation, exhibiting efficient exploration and increasing success by +40% over standard distillation. Overall, it provides a simple yet surprisingly effective framework to learn efficient test-time exploration.
core_methodology: ASTEROID is a student-teacher supervised learning framework that learns test-time exploration by distilling expert actions conditioned on student's on-policy history, enabling efficient exploration under partial observability.
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources but demonstrates effectiveness across various simulated environments and real-world robot manipulation.
alpha_potential: Potential to systematically resolve partial observability in trading strategies, optimize exploration vs. exploitation trade-offs, and reduce sample inefficiency in RL-based approaches.

title: Residual-Based Causal Discovery via Pretrained In-Context Quantile Regression
summary: Residual-based causal discovery assumes that each variable is generated from its parents and an independent noise source. It estimates this noise and tests its independence from candidate causes. For identifiable functions such as additive-noise models (ANMs) and the broader class of location-scale noise models (LSNMs), this principle identifies the causal direction, as only the causal model admits this independence. Existing LSNM methods rely on parametric assumptions to obtain standardized residuals, risking model misspecification. In contrast, the RESIT-framework allows for nonparametric estimation of residuals to iteratively identify sink nodes, but was proposed for ANMs. To close this gap, we propose Loscar, an extension of RESIT to LSNMs that estimates the conditional mean and scale via quantile regression, enabling pretrained tabular foundation models as plug-in estimators. We compare it with a feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) variant, which is consistent given suitable basis functions. Across bivariate and multivariate causal-discovery benchmarks, in-context quantile regression substantially outperforms FGLS with flexible function classes, particularly for multivariate causes.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Loscar, an extension of the RESIT framework to location-scale noise models (LSNMs), using quantile regression to estimate conditional mean and scale, and leverages pretrained tabular foundation models for residual-based causal discovery.
data_sources: The abstract does not specify particular data sources, but the methodology is general and could be applied to financial time series data, including asset returns, macroeconomic indicators, or other market variables.
alpha_potential: The method's ability to identify causal relationships in financial data could help uncover hidden drivers of asset prices or market inefficiencies. This is particularly relevant for factor investing and portfolio optimization where understanding causal structures can improve signal extraction and risk management.
title_cn: 基于残差的因果发现：通过预训练的上下文分位数回归
summary_cn: 本文提出的Loscar方法通过分位数回归估计条件均值和尺度，扩展了RESIT框架，适用于位置-尺度噪声模型（LSNMs）。在金融交易中，该方法可用于识别资产价格或市场变量间的因果结构，有助于因子投资和组合优化中的信号提取与风险管理。

title: What Prediction-Market Contracts Reveal at Launch: Trading Volume and Dispute Risk
summary: Using a near-census of 802,863 resolved markets listed on Polymarket between January 2023 and May 2026, and only information available at listing (the market's title and description, named resolution source, and contract metadata), we predict lifetime trading volume and whether settlement is later disputed. Contract information predicts trading volume well (out-of-sample $R^2 = 0.747$ for log volume), and most of the signal is interpretable: market topic provides the largest gain ($+0.289$ $R^2$ over a $0.220$ contract-feature baseline), wording and resolution-rule design add smaller but measurable improvements ($+0.027$ combined), and neural text models add little beyond the interpretable features. This performance does not survive a period of platform change coinciding with a shift in listing formats: accuracy in predicting whether a market reaches \$1,000 falls from AUC $0.940$ under same-period evaluation to $0.577$ when training on past quarters and testing on later ones. The loss concentrates in markets whose question forms were absent from training (76.9% of test markets; on familiar forms the model still reaches $0.778$), and a decomposition attributes more of it to a changed relationship between contract characteristics and demand than to an outdated mapping from text to features. Dispute predictors are more stable but less precise: launch-time features rank dispute risk far better than chance (AUC $0.78$), yet at a 0.31% base rate precision is too low for case-by-case prediction (average precision $0.012$), so the scores suit ranking groups of markets rather than forecasting individual disputes.
core_methodology: The paper uses interpretable features (market topic, wording, resolution-rule design) and neural text models to predict trading volume and dispute risk in prediction markets. It evaluates the stability of these predictions across temporal changes in the platform.
data_sources: A near-census of 802,863 resolved markets listed on Polymarket between January 2023 and May 2026, including market titles, descriptions, resolution sources, and contract metadata available at listing.
alpha_potential: The method identifies interpretable signals that predict trading volume well (out-of-sample R² = 0.747 for log volume), suggesting potential for market demand forecasting. However, the predictive power diminishes with platform changes, indicating limitations in dynamic environments. Dispute risk prediction, while stable, lacks precision for individual forecasts but may be useful for ranking groups of markets.
title_cn: 预测市场合约上市时的揭示：交易量与争议风险
summary_cn: 该研究利用Polymarket上802,863个已结算市场的上市信息，预测交易量和争议风险。结果显示，合约信息可有效预测交易量（样本外R² = 0.747），且大部分信号可解释。争议风险预测稳定性较高但精确度不足。该方法对量化交易中的需求预测有一定参考价值，但平台变动会影响模型效果。

title: Near Minimax Rate for Quantile Distributional Reinforcement Learning
summary: In this paper, we study quantile distributional policy evaluation, where the return distribution under a given policy is approximated by the quantile Bellman fixed point $\bm\eta_m$. We investigate the statistical accuracy of estimating $\bm\eta_m$ across quantile resolutions under Wasserstein distances. Assuming access to a generative model, we construct a quantile fixed point estimator $\bm\eta_m^{(n)}$ from an empirical Markov decision process and establish non-asymptotic error bounds under Wasserstein distances. When reward densities are uniformly bounded away from zero, we obtain a root-$n$ high-probability bound simultaneously over all resolutions $m$ and all Wasserstein orders $1\le p\le\infty$. When reward densities vanish at the support endpoints, we show that continuity and endpoint monotonicity suffice to preserve the same resolution-independent rate for $1\le p\le2$. For $p>2$, we establish a root-$n$ bound with coefficient $m^{1/2-1/p}$, together with a slower, resolution-independent $n^{-1/p}$ bound for every finite $p>2$. We further obtain resolution-independent $W_\infty$ consistency governed by the continuity modulus of reward quantile functions. To investigate the sharpness of these bounds, we characterize the exact local asymptotic minimax risk at each fixed resolution as the expected Wasserstein-coordinate norm of the efficient Gaussian limit and prove that our estimator attains it. We then examine the resolution dependence of this optimal local risk. A regular one-state instance has resolution-independent local risk constants, whereas a single endpoint-vanishing two-state instance exhibits growth of order $m^{1/2-1/p}$, up to logarithmic factors along a resolution subsequence, for every $p>2$.
core_methodology: Quantile distributional policy evaluation using Wasserstein distances and quantile Bellman fixed points in Markov decision processes
data_sources: Theoretical approach with potential application to reward distributions in trading strategies (requires market data adaptation)
alpha_potential: Potential for estimating extreme value distributions in returns and improving risk-sensitive RL trading strategies
title_cn: 分位数分布强化学习的近极小化率研究
summary_cn: 本文提出的分位数分布算法可用于金融时序数据的极端值分布估计，在风险敏感的强化学习交易系统中有应用潜力。该方法通过分位数Bellman不动点和Wasserstein距离度量，为估计收益分布的尾部风险提供理论框架，适合改进风险管理型量化策略。

title: The Price of Current-Effect Inference in Nonstationary Multi-Armed Bandits
summary: Adaptive experiments use bandit algorithms to favor interventions with higher expected rewards. However, decision-makers also require reliable inference on current treatment effects: differences between intervention and reference-arm mean rewards at the present time, rather than historical averages. These objectives conflict: reward maximization favors better interventions, whereas current-effect inference requires continued exploration of potentially suboptimal interventions as outcomes change over time. We characterize this tradeoff for $K$-arm bandits with H\"older-smooth mean rewards of exponent $\beta\in(0,1]$ and constant $L$. Requiring high-probability simultaneous coverage of all current effects by confidence intervals of width at most $w$, we establish matching minimax bounds, up to logarithmic factors, on expected dynamic regret. Over horizon $T$, our algorithm TRACE (Tracking Rewards and Current Effects) achieves regret of order $\widetilde{O}_{\beta}\left(\sqrt{KT}+K^{\beta/(2\beta+1)}L^{1/(2\beta+1)}T^{(\beta+1)/(2\beta+1)}+Kw^{-2}(1+L^{1/\beta}w^{-1/\beta})\right)$, where the notation hides logarithms and constants depending only on $\beta$. This regret--precision tradeoff separates reward-learning regret from the cost of refreshing current-effect estimates, which remains unavoidable even when one arm is uniformly optimal. An empirical-Bernstein e-process extension adapts exploration to realized prediction errors while preserving worst-case guarantees. When within-block drift is negligible relative to sampling error, all observations, including reward-learning observations, can be reused for asymptotically normal pointwise inference and stronger local stationarity yields local asymptotic efficiency. Finally, we show that regret constraints can prevent honest adaptation to unknown smoothness and support our theory with extensive numerical experiments.
core_methodology: The paper introduces TRACE (Tracking Rewards and Current Effects), an algorithm for multi-armed bandits with non-stationary rewards, focusing on balancing reward maximization with accurate inference of current treatment effects. It uses adaptive experimentation with confidence intervals for current-effect estimation.
data_sources: Synthetic or simulated data for numerical experiments; applicable to any domain with time-varying reward distributions.
alpha_potential: Potential application in dynamic portfolio allocation where asset returns are non-stationary, requiring continuous exploration and exploitation trade-offs. Could be adapted for factor timing strategies in quantitative finance.
title_cn: 非稳态多臂老虎机中当前效应推断的代价
summary_cn: 该论文提出TRACE算法，用于处理奖励非平稳的多臂老虎机问题，平衡奖励最大化与当前效应准确推断。在量化交易中，可应用于动态资产配置和因子择时策略，适应市场变化并持续优化投资决策。

title: Multi-Label Sentiment Analysis on 100 Languages with Dynamic Weighting for Label Imbalance
summary: We investigate cross-lingual sentiment analysis, which has attracted significant attention due to its applications in various areas including market research, politics and social sciences. In particular, we introduce a sentiment analysis framework in multi-label setting as it obeys Plutchik's wheel of emotions. We introduce a novel dynamic weighting method that balances the contribution from each class during training, unlike previous static weighting methods that assign non-changing weights based on their class frequency. Moreover, we adapt the focal loss that favors harder instances from single-label object recognition literature to our multi-label setting. Furthermore, we derive a method to choose optimal class-specific thresholds that maximize the macro-f1 score in linear time complexity. Through an extensive set of experiments, we show that our method obtains the state-of-the-art performance in 7 of 9 metrics in 3 different languages using a single model compared to the common baselines and the best-performing methods in the SemEval competition. We publicly share our code for our model, which can perform sentiment analysis in 100 languages, to facilitate further research.
core_methodology: Multi-label sentiment analysis framework employing dynamic class weighting and adapted focal loss for handling hard instances, with optimized class-specific threshold selection
data_sources: Text data across multiple languages (support for 100 languages), applicable to financial news, social media, and earnings call transcripts
alpha_potential: Potential for cross-lingual sentiment signals in international markets and multi-dimensional emotion analysis of market participants (beyond simple positive/negative sentiment)
title_cn: 基于动态标签权重平衡的百种语言多标签情感分析方法
summary_cn: 本文提出的动态权重多标签情感分析框架可处理包括金融文本在内的跨语言内容，其优化的阈值选择和困难样本处理能力有助于提取更精准的市场情绪信号。该方法在投资决策支持系统和跨国资产配置舆情监控中有应用价值。

title: PRISM: Prompt-Refined In-Context System Modelling for Financial Retrieval
summary: Deploying LLMs for financial information retrieval demands accuracy, cost efficiency, and reproducibility, yet most approaches require expensive fine-tuning. PRISM is a training-free framework that composes three deployable modules (prompt engineering, in-context learning, and a candidate refinement module) with a boundary-condition study of multi-agent coordination for financial document retrieval. On FiQA-2018, stacked reranking and $k$-reciprocal encoding raise Recall@100 from 0.7783 to 0.8326. On FinAgentBench, a Cohere-refined top-50 pool yields a higher observed end-to-end NDCG@5, below this evaluation's minimum detectable effect, while cutting per-query cost by about 35%. Added complexity does not always pay off: $k$-reciprocal encoding stops helping once the upstream stage is already high-recall, and multi-agent coordination is not a default for fine-grained chunk ranking. Matched pairs that hold prompt, model, and exemplars fixed lose 0.0702 and 0.0681 combined NDCG@5 to their single-path controls, and the whole gap sits at the chunk stage. We release an expert-annotated FinAgentBench evaluation set, together with a label-robustness sweep over 16 alternative ground-truth constructions, restoring a reproducible evaluation path after the original evaluator went offline. Without fine-tuning, PRISM placed third on the official FinAgentBench private leaderboard (leaderboard basis, NDCG@5 0.71181), reaches NDCG@10 0.6197 on FiQA-2018, and 98% accuracy on FinanceBench. We report per-query latency, token, and dollar accounting across roughly 40 configurations, present the quality-cost-latency Pareto frontier, and introduce FACET, a transparent SLA-specific scalarization for choosing among non-dominated configurations. Code and dataset are released at https://bit.ly/prism-ailens.
core_methodology: PRISM is a training-free framework combining prompt engineering, in-context learning, and candidate refinement for financial information retrieval. It employs stacked reranking and k-reciprocal encoding to improve recall rates.
data_sources: FiQA-2018, FinAgentBench, and FinanceBench datasets for evaluating financial document retrieval performance.
alpha_potential: The framework improves accuracy and cost-efficiency in financial information retrieval, which could enhance quantitative strategies by providing better data inputs for decision-making. However, the direct translation to alpha generation is limited as it focuses on retrieval rather than predictive modeling.
title_cn: PRISM：金融检索中基于提示优化的上下文系统建模
summary_cn: PRISM是一种无需训练的框架，通过结合提示工程、上下文学习和候选精炼模块，提高金融信息检索的准确性和成本效率。该方法在多个金融数据集上表现出色，显著降低查询成本，并适用于多种配置。虽然主要用于检索而非预测，但其高效的数据处理能力可为量化交易提供更优质的信息输入。

title: Extending ROC Analysis to Uncertainty-Aware Risk Prediction with an Interval-Based AUC (iAUC)
summary: In high-stakes risk prediction, interval-valued predictions provide a natural way to represent predictive uncertainty. However, standard evaluation tools such as the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve and the area under the curve (AUC) are designed for point-valued predictions and do not capture how uncertainty affects discrimination performance. To address this gap, we develop an uncertainty-aware ROC framework and corresponding interval-based AUC (iAUC) metrics for evaluating the performance of interval-valued risk predictions. The framework constructs two ROC-style curves with associated areas $\mathrm{AUC}_L$ and $\mathrm{AUC}_U$, and shows that these quantities induce a three-region decomposition of positive-negative rankings into confidently correct, ambiguous, and confidently incorrect orderings. Under valid class-conditional coverage, $\mathrm{AUC}_L$ and $\mathrm{AUC}_U$, together with the pairwise miscoverage rate, provide theoretical bounds on the optimal AUC, linking interval coverage to achievable discrimination. The framework is compatible with a range of methods for quantifying epistemic uncertainty in risk prediction, including Bayesian, bootstrap, and ensemble-based procedures, and provides a practical way to compare predictive models and interval-generation methods. Experiments on clinical benchmark data and MIMIC-IV mortality prediction show that models with similar point AUC can have different uncertainty-aware ranking profiles, and that the proposed decomposition can support risk-aware model selection and threshold-based abstention.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an uncertainty-aware ROC framework with interval-based AUC (iAUC) metrics to evaluate interval-valued risk predictions, including confidently correct, ambiguous, and confidently incorrect orderings. It also provides theoretical bounds on the optimal AUC under valid class-conditional coverage.
data_sources: Clinical benchmark data and MIMIC-IV mortality prediction data were used in the experiments.
alpha_potential: The framework could be adapted to financial risk prediction models where uncertainty quantification is crucial, potentially improving model selection and risk-aware decision-making in trading strategies.
title_cn: 拓展ROC分析至不确定性感知的风险预测：基于区间的AUC（iAUC）
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一个不确定性感知的ROC框架和区间AUC（iAUC）指标，用于评估区间风险预测的性能。该框架理论上限定了AUC的边界，并通过三区域分解（确信正确、模糊和确信错误的排序）支持风险感知的模型选择和阈值弃权决策。

title: Learning to Allocate Resources with Censored Feedback
summary: We study an online resource allocation problem in which at each round, a budget $B$ must be allocated across $K$ arms under censored feedback. An arm yields a reward if and only if two conditions are satisfied: (i) the arm is activated according to an arm-specific Bernoulli random variable with unknown parameter, and (ii) the allocated budget exceeds a random threshold drawn from a parametric distribution with unknown parameter. Over $T$ rounds, the learner must jointly estimate the unknown parameters and allocate the budget so as to maximize cumulative reward facing the exploration--exploitation trade-off. We prove a worst-case regret lower bound $\Omega(\sqrt{T})$ for the general model, even with known uniform threshold distributions. We then propose RA-UCB, an optimistic algorithm that leverages non-trivial parameter estimation and confidence bounds. When the budget $B$ is known at the beginning of each round, RA-UCB achieves a regret bound of order $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T})$, and even $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{poly}\text{-}\log T)$ under stronger assumptions. As for unknown, round dependent budget, we introduce \texttt{MG-UCB}, which allows within-round switching and infinitesimal allocations, and matches the regret guarantees of RA-UCB. We then validate our theoretical results through experiments on real-world datasets.
core_methodology: Online resource allocation algorithm (RA-UCB and MG-UCB) with censored feedback, leveraging non-trivial parameter estimation and confidence bounds to maximize cumulative reward under budget constraints.
data_sources: Real-world datasets (unspecified but implied by the abstract), likely involving scenarios where budget allocation under uncertainty is critical, such as ad placements or clinical trials, though financial applications could include budget-constrained portfolio optimization.
alpha_potential: Potential application in budget-constrained portfolio optimization, where the algorithm could dynamically allocate limited capital across assets with uncertain returns and activation conditions. The method could exploit market inefficiencies by balancing exploration and exploitation in uncertain environments.
title_cn: 基于截尾反馈的资源分配学习
summary_cn: 本文研究了一种在线资源分配问题，通过RA-UCB和MG-UCB算法，在截尾反馈下动态分配预算以最大化累计奖励。该方法可应用于预算约束下的投资组合优化，通过探索-利用权衡在不确定市场中动态分配资本，具有潜在的阿尔法收益机会。

title: Flow Matching Policy Optimization with Mirror Descent and Entropy Constraints
summary: Balancing policy expressiveness with the exploration-exploitation trade-off is a core challenge in online Reinforcement Learning (RL). While Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE)-based diffusion policies can represent complex, multimodal action distributions, they suffer from two critical limitations: their stochastic reverse processes render entropy intractable (necessitating heuristic exploration), and computing policy gradients through long denoising chains is expensive and unstable. In this work, we show that ODE-based flow matching inherently resolves these issues by enabling both simulation-free policy optimization and tractable entropy computation. Building on this, we introduce Flow Matching Policy Optimization with Mirror Descent and Entropy Constraints (FMER). Our framework exploits this insight in three ways. First, we derive an analytic entropy objective that corrects for the density distortion caused by the $\tanh$ transformation (mapping an unbounded latent space to bounded actions), thereby facilitating entropy-constrained policy optimization. Second, we theoretically establish that minimizing an advantage-weighted conditional flow matching loss acts as a simulation-free surrogate for policy mirror descent. This steers the velocity field toward high-value regions while entirely avoiding backpropagation through the ODE solver. Finally, we dynamically tune the mirror descent temperature based on the effective sample size to enforce a robust trust region during training. Empirical evaluations demonstrate that FMER achieves superior performance on the challenging sparse-reward FrankaKitchen environment, while maintaining competitive results across standard dense-reward MuJoCo benchmarks. Code is available at https://github.com/gtanaelle/FMER.git.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Flow Matching Policy Optimization with Mirror Descent and Entropy Constraints (FMER), a novel ODE-based flow matching approach for online Reinforcement Learning (RL). It enables simulation-free policy optimization, tractable entropy computation, and dynamic temperature tuning to enforce a robust trust region during training.
data_sources: The methodology was evaluated on sparse-reward FrankaKitchen and dense-reward MuJoCo benchmarks, which might serve as proxies for real-world trading environments with different reward structures.
alpha_potential: This approach could potentially be applied to trading strategy optimization where balancing exploration-exploitation trade-offs is crucial, particularly in market conditions with sparse rewards (e.g., rare significant price movements). The dynamic temperature tuning based on effective sample size might help maintain robust financial risk-adjusted returns over time.
title_cn: 基于镜像下降与熵约束的流匹配策略优化
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新型ODE(常微分方程)基础的流匹配策略优化方法FMER，解决了传统SDE方法存在的熵计算难、训练不稳定等问题。通过创新的模拟自由策略优化机制和动态温度调节技术，该方法在稀疏奖励环境下表现出色。在量化交易领域，该技术可应用于需要平衡探索-利用的关键策略优化场景，特别是处理市场重大但稀少的价格变动机会。其自动维持稳健信任区域的特性有助于保持长期稳定的风险调整后收益。

title: Sequential sparse Gaussian process quantile regression
summary: Quantile regression aims to estimate the conditional quantiles of a response variable from observed data. In a Bayesian setting, Gaussian process quantile regression provides uncertainty quantification but faces significant computational challenges due to the nonconjugacy of the asymmetric Laplace likelihood and the cost of posterior inference. We develop a sparse Gaussian process framework in which the quantile function is represented through a reduced set of inducing variables and posterior inference is performed using a Laplace approximation. A decomposition of the predictive uncertainty into conditional-prior and posterior-induced variance components is then exploited to drive two complementary adaptive mechanisms: inducing-input infilling and data acquisition. These mechanisms are combined within a sequential algorithm that allocates computational effort toward the dominant source of predictive uncertainty and adaptively controls model complexity. Numerical experiments on benchmark problems demonstrate the accuracy of the Laplace approximation, the benefits of variance-based inducing-input placement, and the effectiveness of the proposed sequential enrichment strategy compared with predefined data-acquisition strategies. The method is finally applied to ship seakeeping under forecast uncertainty, where it outperforms a replication-based counterpart from the literature under limited simulation budgets.
core_methodology: Sequential sparse Gaussian process quantile regression with adaptive inducing-point placement and data acquisition
data_sources: Generic benchmark data (paper's focus is methodological), potentially applicable to financial time series
alpha_potential: Could be adapted for probabilistic forecasting in volatility modeling or conditional quantile estimation for risk management strategies
title_cn: 序列稀疏高斯过程分位数回归
summary_cn: 该论文提出的自适应稀疏高斯过程分位数回归方法，通过动态优化计算资源分配，可应用于金融时间序列的条件分位数预测。其不确定性分解机制对于波动率建模和风险管理策略具有潜在价值，特别适合需要有限计算预算的场景。

title: Adaptive Entangled Neurons in the Brain and Natural Intelligence Simulations for Artificial General Intelligence
summary: Understanding the brain's mechanisms is crucial in neuroscience, particularly for simulating natural intelligence and advancing artificial general intelligence (AGI). Liu et al. (2024) and Deco et al. (2025) propose that quantum entanglement may underlie the synchronization of millions of neurons, introducing the Liu-Chen-Ao (LCA) hypothesis of entangled nerve fibers. However, directly testing this idea remains challenging. Here we employ a nonlocal many-body wave equation, introducing a generalized probability-wave framework to model collective behaviors among adaptive, interacting agents, particles, or neurons. This approach enables testable eigenmodes, offering an indirect means of examining the LCA hypothesis by observing patterns in collective trading behaviors. These patterns, rooted in behavioral psychology, are thought to mirror the internal brain's decision-making and underlying mechanisms. Our analysis of Chinese intraday stock market data shows that adaptive entangled game modes explain 82%-94% of decision patterns, sharply contrasting neoclassical finance predictions assuming independent rational agents. Additionally, 2-12% of actions adapt to news, events, and environmental changes, marked by rapid equilibrium shifts, while truly independent behaviors make up less than 5%. These results empirically support the LCA hypothesis and underscore the need to simulate the brain's mechanisms and generate adaptive, entangled modules for AGI. They also expose the shortcomings of conventional artificial neural networks (ANNs) that depend on vast, opaque parameters. By combining ANN-based AI with probability-wave-based entangled brain simulations, machine learning enables the creation of human-like processing units (HPUs). Such HPUs promise more efficient and robust AGI, particularly for embodied intelligence and robotics.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a nonlocal many-body wave equation and generalized probability-wave framework to model collective behaviors among adaptive, interacting agents, particles, or neurons, particularly in financial markets. This approach aims to examine patterns in collective trading behaviors that may mirror brain's decision-making mechanisms.
data_sources: Chinese intraday stock market data
alpha_potential: The methodology suggests that market behaviors are largely influenced by collective, entangled decision-making patterns rather than independent rational agents, which could potentially be exploited by identifying and predicting these patterns. The study found that 82%-94% of decision patterns can be explained by adaptive entangled game modes, offering a new perspective on market inefficiencies.
title_cn: 大脑中的自适应纠缠神经元与自然智能模拟在人工通用智能中的应用
summary_cn: 本研究通过非局域多体波方程和概率波框架，分析中国股市日内数据，揭示市场决策模式主要由集体纠缠行为主导（占82%-94%），而非理性独立决策。这为开发新型交易策略提供了理论依据，特别是在识别群体行为和快速市场均衡转变方面具有应用潜力。

title: Pessimistic Latent Task-aware Optimization for Robust Offline Meta-Reinforcement Learning
summary: Context-based offline meta-reinforcement learning (COMRL) has advanced almost entirely through better task representations, which separate task identity from artifacts of the behavior policy so that the latent reflects the task alone. The implicit expectation has been that a clean representation will transfer to out-of-support (parameter-extrapolation) tasks. On such a task, however, the encoder produces a latent outside the training support, where the policy has never been trained. We address this gap with Pessimistic Latent Task-aware Optimization (PLATO), which exposes the policy to off-support latents during training. PLATO assumes a mild manifold hypothesis: task latents lie on a low-dimensional manifold, and out-of-support tasks lie farther from the training centroid. It exploits this geometry by perturbing inferred latents outward from the centroid to synthesize counterfactual tasks. A learned decoder ensemble then rolls out short trajectories at each perturbed latent, and the policy is updated on the imagined transitions under a pessimism weight that down-weights steps on which the ensemble disagrees. We prove that the perturbation leaves the training support by a controllable margin and that the out-of-support generalization gap is bounded by the same perturbation reach, and we give explicit conditions, verified empirically, under which the epistemic disagreement at the perturbed latent stays bounded away from zero. On eight MuJoCo continuous-control benchmarks, PLATO consistently improves out-of-support returns over strong COMRL baselines while remaining competitive on in-distribution tasks. Our code is available at https://github.com/deephoony/plato.
core_methodology: PLATO introduces a pessimistic latent task-aware optimization method for offline meta-reinforcement learning, focusing on improving generalization to out-of-support tasks via latent space perturbations and ensemble-based trajectory imagination.
data_sources: Benchmarked on eight MuJoCo continuous-control environments (not financial data, but methodology could potentially transfer to financial time-series data).
alpha_potential: Methodology could potentially be adapted to improve robustness in trading strategy generalization across different market regimes, particularly for out-of-sample periods where traditional strategies fail.
title_cn: 稳健离线元强化学习的悲观潜在任务感知优化
summary_cn: PLATO通过潜在空间扰动和集成学习的方法，在任务表示中引入悲观权重优化，提升离线强化学习模型在非支持分布任务上的泛化能力。该方法可潜在应用于金融时间序列分析，提升交易策略在市场状态突变时的稳健性。

title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
summary: Momentum is central to stochastic optimization in deep learning, including the training of large language models. Classical momentum methods typically rely on a fast exponential moving average (EMA) scheme, which discounts past gradients on a fixed timescale and may underweight older gradients that remain informative. This creates a trade-off between retaining long-term history and adapting to recent changes. We introduce Hybrid Momentum (HyM), which combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum. The former assigns weights proportional to the gradients' iteration indices and retains a growing span of history, while the latter emphasizes recent gradients. This hybrid construction is modular and can be combined with adaptive preconditioning and other update transformations. In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales. Across image classification, machine translation, and language modeling, HyM and HyMUON match or improve upon strong baselines. HyMUON improves over Muon on IWSLT14, and in both the 100k- and 600k-step GPT-2 124M OpenWebText regimes. For LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.
core_methodology: Hybrid Momentum (HyM) combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum to balance long-term history retention with recent gradient emphasis. HyMUON extends this with Newton--Schulz orthogonalization.
data_sources: Primarily tested on image classification, machine translation, and language modeling tasks (e.g., IWSLT14, GPT-2 on OpenWebText, LLaMA-1.3B on C4)
alpha_potential: The methodology could be adapted for financial time series momentum strategies where balancing long-term trends with recent market movements is valuable. Potential applications in portfolio optimization or adaptive trading systems.
title_cn: 混合动量方法在深度学习模型优化中的应用
summary_cn: 本文提出的混合动量方法(HyM)结合线性加权和几何贴现动量，可潜在应用于金融时间序列分析。通过平衡长期趋势和近期变动，该方法可能改进交易策略中的动量因子计算，特别适合需要动态调整权重的多时间尺度投资组合优化。

title: The Sample Complexity of Multiple Change Point Identification under Bandit Feedback
summary: We study multiple change point localization under bandit feedback. An unknown piecewise-constant function on a compact interval can be queried sequentially at adaptively chosen inputs, and each query returns a noisy evaluation of the function. The goal is to identify a prescribed number of discontinuities, known as change points, within a target precision $\eta$ and confidence level $1-\delta$, while using as few samples as possible. We propose an adaptive algorithm that first detects intervals likely to contain change points and then refines their locations to precision $\eta$. We establish non-asymptotic upper bounds on its sample budget, together with corresponding lower bounds. Prior work shows that jump magnitudes alone determine the asymptotic sample complexity as $\delta\to 0$. We reveal that this picture is incomplete beyond this regime. We demonstrate, both empirically and theoretically, that for general $\delta$ and $\eta$, the complexity is jointly governed by the jumps and the relative positions of the change points.
core_methodology: The paper presents an adaptive algorithm for identifying multiple change points in piecewise-constant functions under bandit feedback. The approach involves detection of intervals containing change points followed by precise localization, with theoretical guarantees on sample complexity.
data_sources: Theoretically applicable to any time-series data with abrupt structural changes (e.g., asset prices, volatility regimes). The abstract doesn't specify real financial data but the methodology is general.
alpha_potential: Could help detect regime changes in markets faster with limited samples, potentially improving timing of momentum strategies or risk management systems. However, practical trading applications would require significant adaptation to financial time series.
title_cn: 强盗反馈下多重变点识别的样本复杂性研究
summary_cn: 本文提出一种自适应算法，用于在强盗反馈条件下高效识别分段常数函数中的多重变点。该技术可应用于金融市场结构突变检测，潜在改进交易时机选择和风险管理。算法通过先检测可能包含变点的区间，再精确定位的方式优化样本使用效率，但需针对金融数据特点进行专门适配。

title: To Retain or to Adapt? Generalizing Continual Learning
summary: The Continual Learning (CL) literature has long been driven by the goal of mitigating catastrophic forgetting. This objective rests on an often unstated assumption: that a lifelong learner should approximate the Joint-Task Learning (JTL) solution and retain all previously acquired knowledge. We challenge this retention-centered premise, arguing that in non-stationary environments prioritizing retention can impede real-time adaptation. Shifting the focus to the Average Lifelong Error (ALE), we formalize CL as an online optimization problem governed by the interaction between environmental and learning dynamics. We introduce Transfer Efficiency as a quantitative measure of the tension between Instability, the bias inherited from conflicting past experience, and Transient Error, the optimization cost of learning new tasks from scratch. Under mild convergence conditions, holding across linear and neural network models, this decomposition yields a Critical Task Duration: a closed-form threshold beyond which historical knowledge transitions from a warm-start advantage to an optimization liability whenever retention induces a positive stationary bias. We validate these theoretical predictions on continual image classification and reinforcement learning benchmarks. Finally, by connecting continual learning to the online learning framework of predictable sequences, we show that JTL is only one instance of a broader family of objectives, and we propose a new general class of continual learning algorithms, which we call Predictive Continual Learning. Predictive CL algorithms optimize expected future performance under an explicit, dynamically updated model of future tasks. As a proof of concept, we analyze a Window algorithm that interpolates between JTL and Independent-Task Learning (ITL), outperforming both under controlled distributional drift.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a new approach to Continual Learning (CL) by shifting focus from retention to adaptation, formalizing CL as an online optimization problem. It proposes Transfer Efficiency as a measure of the tension between past knowledge and new learning, and introduces Predictive Continual Learning algorithms optimized for future performance under dynamically updated task models.
data_sources: Benchmarked on continual image classification and reinforcement learning tasks, suggesting potential application to financial time series and market data.
alpha_potential: The methodology could enhance adaptive trading strategies by dynamically balancing the retention of past market knowledge with real-time adaptation to new market conditions, potentially capturing alpha in non-stationary financial environments.
title_cn: 保留还是适应？广义持续学习
summary_cn: 本研究挑战了持续学习中传统的知识保留假设，提出了一种动态适应方法，通过在线优化和未来性能预测，优化非稳态环境下的学习过程。在金融交易中，该方法可应用于动态调整交易策略，平衡历史知识和实时市场适应，从而在多变市场条件下捕捉阿尔法收益。

title: Causal Discovery via Transformed Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces
summary: We propose Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces (LRQS), a bivariate causal model in which, in the causal direction, an unknown monotone transformation of the conditional quantile surface admits a low-rank functional decomposition. LRQS subsumes location-scale noise models and post-nonlinear heteroscedastic noise models, while allowing multiple quantile bases to represent changes beyond location-scale effects. We prove generic identifiability of LRQS: the transformed quantile surface is low rank in the causal direction, whereas reverse representability under the corresponding constraints occurs only for exceptional, fine-tuned cause marginals. We provide a nonparametric causal score using a fitting procedure that alternates between rank-constrained approximation of discretized quantile surfaces and isotonic estimation of the unknown monotone transformation. Experiments on synthetic mechanisms with higher-rank distributional shape variation and strong nonlinear distortions, together with standard bivariate benchmarks, show that LRQS is especially effective when conditional distributional shape or observation distortion goes beyond existing location-scale assumptions.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Low-Rank Quantile Surfaces (LRQS), a causal model where a transformed conditional quantile surface has a low-rank functional decomposition in the causal direction. It involves nonparametric causal scoring by alternating between rank-constrained quantile surface approximation and isotonic transformation estimation.
data_sources: The methodology is generic and could be applied to any bivariate financial data, such as asset returns versus macroeconomic indicators or paired asset relationships. The abstract mentions tests on synthetic mechanisms and standard bivariate benchmarks.
alpha_potential: This method could potentially identify causal relationships in financial markets beyond simple location-scale models, uncovering hidden causal drivers of asset price movements or risk factor interactions. The transformation approach may better capture nonlinear dependencies in financial data.
title_cn: 通过变换低秩分位数曲面进行因果发现
summary_cn: 本文提出的低秩分位数曲面(LRQS)方法能够发现超越传统位置-规模假设的因果关系，在金融领域可能用于识别资产间的非线性因果关系和市场风险的潜在驱动因素。该技术通过变换后的低秩分位数分解，可处理金融数据中常见的高度非线性依赖关系。

title: The Data Differentiator Framework (DDF): Quantifying Marginal Data Value with Information-Theoretic and Game-Theoretic Measures in an Agentic Evaluation Pipeline (SDSAE)
summary: In data-rich enterprises the hard question is not whether a candidate dataset is good in isolation, but whether it adds information beyond what the organization already holds, and whether that increment is worth its price. We present the Data Differentiator Framework (DDF), a composite scoring method for candidate data assets that combines (i) a mutual-information-based redundancy penalty against the existing portfolio, (ii) a cost-normalized, significance-gated marginal utility score derived from an ablation study, and (iii) explicit governance inputs (trust, identity resolution quality, strategic weights) set by the business. The framework is executed by a staged pipeline, the Strategic Data Sourcing Agent Ecosystem (SDSAE), that short-circuits expensive model-retraining steps for assets failing governance or redundancy gates. Conceptually, the DDF extends the relevance-minus-redundancy principle of mRMR feature selection from the feature level to the asset level, and adds cost normalization, a statistical significance gate, and governance terms that per-sample valuation methods such as Data Shapley do not model. We validate the framework on the public credit-card fraud benchmark (284,807 transactions) with five constructed candidate assets spanning the redundancy spectrum. Only the genuinely differentiated asset passes the significance gate ($\Delta$AUC = +0.0029, DeLong $p = 1.4\times 10^{-9}$, Holm-corrected $p = 7.2\times 10^{-9}$) and receives an acquire recommendation (DDS = +0.663); the fully redundant asset scores lowest (DDS = -0.135). The recommendation is stable across 19 of 22 admissible strategic-weight configurations and across all decision thresholds in [0.15, 0.66]. We state clearly which quantities in the case study are computed from data and which are simulated governance inputs, and we discuss the design limits of a single-dataset evaluation.
core_methodology: A composite scoring method combining mutual-information-based redundancy penalty, cost-normalized marginal utility score with statistical significance gate, and governance inputs, applied through a staged evaluation pipeline.
data_sources: Public credit-card fraud benchmark (284,807 transactions) with five constructed candidate assets spanning the redundancy spectrum.
alpha_potential: Potential to identify differentiated data assets that can enhance model performance beyond existing datasets, possibly applicable to trading signal generation or risk management.
title_cn: 数据差异化框架（DDF）：在代理评估管道中使用信息论和博弈论度量量化边际数据价值（SDSAE）
summary_cn: 该框架通过结合冗余惩罚、边际效用评分和治理输入，评估新数据资产的价值，适用于金融领域的数据选择和模型优化，可能提升量化交易策略的表现。

title: Interpretable Cutting Plane Selection for Mixed-Integer Linear Programming Using Genetic Programming
summary: Cutting planes (cuts) remove fractional solutions from mixed-integer linear programs (MILPs) without excluding any feasible integer solutions, making them a key ingredient in modern MILP solvers. Current state-of-the-art solvers rely on fine-tuned handcrafted cut strategies, which, despite their effectiveness, remain inherently static and can be suboptimal. More recently, learning-based approaches have been proposed to design adaptive cut strategies; however, most of these methods are based on neural networks, offering limited interpretability and providing no guarantees of convergence. In this paper, we propose \emph{Genetic Programming and Statistics-based Cut Selection} (GPSCS), the first learning-based framework that explicitly generalizes handcrafted cut selection heuristics into a fully interpretable policy. First, a genetic programming model evolves a symbolic scoring function that ranks candidate cuts using features derived from the cuts and the solving context. Second, a lightweight statistics-based mechanism adaptively determines the number of top-ranked cuts to add at each separation round by detecting significant score dropouts. We evaluate GPSCS within the SCIP solver on seven classes of synthetic and real-world benchmark instances, with a strong emphasis on generalization: evaluation instances are on average 41 times harder than those used for training. Experimental results show that GPSCS improves average solving time by $6\%$ compared to SCIP's default cut selection strategy and achieves a two-fold speedup over both a recent neural-network-based approach and a no-cut baseline, demonstrating strong robustness and generalization across heterogeneous MILP families.
core_methodology: Genetic Programming and Statistics-based Cut Selection (GPSCS) for Mixed-teger Linear Programming (MILP)
data_sources: Synthetic and real-world benchmark instances (non-financial domains)
alpha_potential: Potential for optimizing portfolio construction and execution algorithms through more efficient integer programming solutions. Likely involves solving combinatorial optimization problems with constraints (though not directly demonstrated on financial data)
title_cn: 基于遗传编程的混合整数线性规划可解释切割平面选择方法
summary_cn: 本研究提出的遗传编程统计切割选择框架(GPSCS)可优化整数规划求解效率，在组合优化、约束条件下订单执行等量化金融中的NP难问题领域具有潜在应用价值。该方法的可解释性特征对策略透明度要求高的交易场景尤为重要。

title: EPIC: Rethinking Trust Regions for Autoregressive LLM Policies via Exact-KL Prefix Importance-Ratio Clipping
summary: Reinforcement learning (RL) based on PPO-style clipping has become an effective approach to improving the reasoning capabilities of large language models (LLMs). However, standard token-level clipping measures policy change only through the conditional probability of the current token, while the prefix conditioning context is itself generated by the policy. This mismatch becomes especially consequential in long-response and off-policy training. We reformulate autoregressive generation as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and derive its performance-difference identity under behavior-policy sampling. The resulting change of measure identifies the cumulative likelihood ratio of the generated prefix as the exact importance weight for each stepwise policy-improvement term. Starting from the monotonic-improvement principle of trust-region policy optimization, we then construct a prefix-level trust region using the exact reverse-KL coordinate $r-1-\log r$, whose behavior-policy expectation equals the corresponding prefix-distribution KL divergence. This yields EPIC, a PPO-style sequence-clipping method that directly regulates prefix-level policy drift without relying on a local quadratic approximation or expert-routing replay. Experiments on off-policy reinforcement learning with a sparse mixture-of-experts language model show that EPIC consistently outperforms standard and sequence-level clipping baselines across mathematical-reasoning benchmarks, while remaining competitive with routing-replay-based alternatives. Code is available at https://github.com/LiChengxi666/EPIC.
core_methodology: EPIC introduces a PPO-style sequence-clipping method for autoregressive LLM policies, using exact-KL prefix importance-ratio clipping to regulate prefix-level policy drift. The method reformulates autoregressive generation as a finite-horizon Markov decision process and employs a trust-region approach for policy optimization.
data_sources: Experiments are conducted on mathematical-reasoning benchmarks, but the methodology is neutral and can be adapted to financial text (e.g., earnings reports, news sentiment).
alpha_potential: The method could potentially improve AI trading agents by better regulating policy drift in sequential decision-making tasks (e.g., portfolio rebalancing, trade execution automation). However, explicit financial applications are not demonstrated.
title_cn: EPIC：通过精确KL前缀重要性比率剪裁重新思考自回归LLM策略的信任区域
summary_cn: 本文提出的EPIC方法改进了PPO算法在长序列任务中的策略优化，通过对前缀KL散度的精确控制来稳定强化学习过程。在量化交易中可能应用于基于LLM的交易决策系统优化，但需要针对金融时序数据进行适配开发。

title: Extreme Low-State Quantized Transformer for Electricity-Load Forecasting
summary: Aggressive low-state weight quantization can substantially reduce neural-network representational flexibility, making predictive performance difficult to preserve when only a few discrete weight states are available. We investigate this regime for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting using 3-, 5-, 7-, and 16-state weight quantization across feed-forward-only and attention-plus-feed-forward quantization. Two tasks predict either the next hour or the next 24 hours from the preceding 48 hours across two co-primary electricity-consumption datasets. Direct post-training quantization (PTQ) increased mean normalized root-mean-square error (NRMSE) relative to full precision by 6.25 and 7.04 percentage points in Datasets A and B, whereas quantization-aware fine-tuning (QAT-FT) recovered approximately 90.2% and 94.5% of these penalties. Quantization-aware training from random initialization (Scratch-QAT) also produced competitive low-state solutions, with particularly favorable behavior at three states. We further introduce accumulated-update thresholding, which accumulates optimizer-proposed weight changes before commitment. Relative to paired Scratch-QAT controls, this reduced committed shadow-weight updates by approximately 99.7% and discrete state transitions by approximately 77--80%, while mean NRMSE changed by only +0.042 and +0.197 percentage points. These results show that useful Transformer forecasting can be retained under highly discrete weight representations while strongly suppressing target-state activity, supporting a prospective route toward compact, low-activity edge forecasting using multilevel synaptic devices.
core_methodology: Investigation of low-state weight quantization for Transformer-based electricity-load forecasting, comparing post-training quantization (PTQ), quantization-aware fine-tuning (QAT-FT), and quantization-aware training from random initialization (Scratch-QAT). Introduces accumulated-update thresholding to reduce weight updates and state transitions.
data_sources: Two co-primary electricity-consumption datasets.
alpha_potential: Limited direct alpha potential for financial markets, but the methodology of extreme low-state quantization could be adapted for edge computing in high-frequency trading or other latency-sensitive applications.

title: JaxMARL-BC: Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Macroeconomic Modelling, in Seconds
summary: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) offers a principled way of populating simulated economies with many heterogeneous decision makers. Its adoption, pioneered in finance, has nonetheless been slow in macroeconomics because of two main limitations: the lack of a shared frame of reference connecting MARL systems to dynamic stochastic general equilibrium (DSGE) models the profession already trusts, and the very long training times. The first limitation was recently addressed by the Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning Business Cycle (MARL-BC), which places deep RL households in a real business cycle economy and reduces to classic DSGE models in specific limits. Here we address the second limitation. We present JaxMARL-BC, a JAX-accelerated simulator that trains MARL-BC economies in seconds (between 75x and 724x faster than the reference implementation), and scales to 200,000 independent learning households. We verify its correctness against the known DSGE limits, characterise its scaling through a simple cost law, and demonstrate its value by a proof-of-concept calibration of an extended model with heterogeneous returns on capital, in a two-hour experiment that would previously have taken over a month. We release JaxMARL-BC as open source.
core_methodology: Multi-agent reinforcement learning (MARL) accelerated with JAX for macroeconomic modeling
data_sources: Simulated economies with heterogeneous agents, no real market data used
alpha_potential: Limited direct trading application; primarily useful for theoretical economic modeling speed improvements

title: Transformers as Generic Deep Neural Networks: Exact Compilation, the Cost of Removing Activation-Activation Products, and Multi-Agent Attention Clustering
summary: Transformers are deployed as a special model class. Neural processing units (NPU) add dedicated operators for attention and normalization, and quantization relies on Transformer-specific algorithms. We show the computation does not force this. Every Transformer block, with attention, LayerNorm and a GELU MLP, compiles exactly into a generic deep neural network built from fixed affine maps, routing and the square, sigmoid and inverse square root, plus GELU or its sigmoid approximation. Without activation-activation products, every transform-wise compilation adds at least $N^2$ scalar nonlinear evaluations per head for dense scores. Keeping that one operation type removes this cost; its elementwise form, present on every surveyed NPU, suffices with the sigmoid and inverse square root. For top-$k$ attention with exchangeable tail scores, we prove that exact or conditional-mean tail mass gives an unbiased, minimum-mean-square-error estimate of the attention distribution, while tail drop is conditionally biased. When queries or agents cluster, centroids choose the keys first, reducing the number of computed scores from $N^2$ to $Nk$ per head. On DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light and Pythia-70M the compiled models match their references with all keys, standard post-training quantization applies, and the exact tail-mass estimate beats tail dropping with half as many keys on DeiT-Tiny and, for $k\le8$, on Pythia-70M.
core_methodology: The paper discusses the compilation of Transformer models into generic deep neural networks, focusing on removing activation-activation products and optimizing attention mechanisms with clustering techniques.
data_sources: The study evaluates methods on DeiT-Tiny, MambaIRv2-Light, and Pythia-70M models, suggesting potential applicability to any data type that can be processed by Transformers.
alpha_potential: Potential improvements in computational efficiency for neural models could indirectly benefit quantitative trading strategies by enabling faster or more efficient processing of financial data.

title: From Common Information to Canonical Correlation Analysis and Beyond: Bridging Information Theory, Signal Processing, and Machine Learning
summary: Many problems in signal processing, machine learning, and neuroimaging provide several jointly observed measurements of one process, each mixing a component common to all of them with a component private to itself, and require the common component to be recovered without supervision. This problem has been studied in several communities, largely independently. Statisticians proposed canonical correlation analysis (CCA), introduced by Hotelling in 1936. Information theorists proposed two notions of common information, due to G\'acs and K\"orner and to Wyner. Engineers developed subspace methods for sensor arrays and multiuser communications to design multiview receivers. This tutorial presents the main results and tools each community developed for this problem in a single exposition, and explains the connections that emerge where they meet, distinguishing exact equivalences from special cases and analogies. We develop the information-theoretic foundation from first principles. We then introduce CCA and its extension to several views, followed by the engineering thread from blind multiuser detection to CCA as a blind receiver. Next, we turn to nonlinear CCA, covering kernel, deep, and probabilistic formulations, the conditions under which the common factor is identifiable, and connections to self-supervised learning. We conclude with a discussion of further extensions and open directions. The exposition is self-contained, so that readers from each of these communities can follow the parts developed by the others.
core_methodology: Focuses on canonical correlation analysis (CCA) and its extensions, including nonlinear variants like kernel, deep, and probabilistic CCA, for extracting common components from multiple data sources
data_sources: Multiple jointly observed measurements (e.g., multi-sensor or multi-view data), applicable to signal processing, neuroimaging, and similar multivariate problems
alpha_potential: Potentially useful for factor analysis or extracting common signals from multiple financial time series, though primarily theoretical in nature

title: GRAIL: From Saliency to Semantics in Time-Series Explanation
summary: Explaining a time-series model requires both locating the evidence and extracting meaningful knowledge from it. Yet a single timestep is not a semantic unit: the meaningful patterns live across many samples, not in any one of them. Per-timestep saliency is therefore noisy, high-dimensional, and unstable. Existing methods address this by introducing fixed-size windows and treating them as independent players in a cooperative game. Evaluating a coalition of such players requires defining a ``baseline'' region, which prior work tackles with fixed counterfactuals (e.g., a flat line, noise, or a spectral surrogate). This choice frequently dominates the resulting explanation, obscuring the model's true decisions. To address these issues, we propose GRAIL, a region-based time-series explanation framework that uses domain-specific intervals, such as the P-wave and the QRS complex of an electrocardiogram (ECG) beat, as players. We describe each region with human-readable features and generate counterfactual baselines with an on-manifold conditional generator. Such a choice of players also admits non-temporal features: static covariates enter as singleton players attributed with the temporal regions on one scale, so a patient's tabular evidence (e.g., age, sex) is weighed directly against the signal. We attribute the predictions to the features via Owen values with common-random-number variance reduction. Experimental results on both synthetic and real data show that the proposed framework produces faithful and robust explanations, evaluated under matched on- and off-manifold operators, offering meaningful knowledge to domain experts.
core_methodology: Region-based time-series explanation framework using domain-specific intervals and human-readable features for counterfactual baselines
data_sources: Primarily tested on synthetic and real electrocardiogram (ECG) data, but methodology could theoretically be adapted to financial time-series
alpha_potential: Potential for identifying meaningful patterns in financial time-series data, but no direct evidence of applicability to market inefficiencies

title: Steering Black-Box Large Language Model Agents with Pitfall Anticipation World Model
summary: Frontier black-box Large Language Model (LLM) agents are proficient at long-horizon reasoning and precise action generation. However, when it comes to a specific agentic task, they have no internalized knowledge of how that particular environment unfolds. A world model offers a natural remedy, providing the agent with environment specific knowledge by foreseeing how the environment will respond to the action it is about to take. Prior world models for LLM agents mainly predict next observations at each step, which is costly and often uninformative because individual observations provide limited task-relevant guidance and not every step requires call for foresight. This raises a key question: what a world model should predict and when should it be invoked for agentic tasks? Our pilot study suggests that world model guidance is most useful when it anticipates pitfalls within a bounded multi-step future. Motivated by this, we introduce Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM), which selectively intervenes when a potential pitfall arises and predicts the impending failure to steer the agent away from it. PAWM is trained in two stages: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) on synthetic data labeled with agent pitfalls, followed by GRPO co-training with a black-box LLM to further optimize it in the target environment. PAWM improves Claude Sonnet 4.5 performance by 24.3% on ScienceWorld and 7.7% on WebArena-Lite, outperforming a range of baselines. These results demonstrate that PAWM provides an effective form of world model guidance for black-box LLM agents.
core_methodology: Pitfall Anticipation World Model (PAWM) for black-box LLM agents, involving two-stage training with synthetic data and GRPO co-training
data_sources: Synthetic data for training and evaluation on ScienceWorld and WebArena-Lite
alpha_potential: Potential for error reduction in LLM-based decision processes, but no direct financial market application demonstrated

title: SAFTER: Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability for Robust Reinforcement Learning under Distribution Shift
summary: Learning safe policies that generalize to unseen environments is difficult under bounded actuation, where an unsafe decision may become unrecoverable. Conventional control barrier function (CBF) filters enforce only instantaneous safety and ignore future recoverability. We propose SAFTER (Safety-Aware Filtering Through Explicit Recoverability), which embeds a differentiable, closed-form backup-CBF filter into Soft Actor-Critic training. SAFTER unifies current safety, finite-horizon backup safety, terminal recoverability, and input admissibility into a single differentiable certificate. Its CBF condition yields an exact minimum-intervention projection without iterative online optimization. In quadruped navigation, SAFTER reaches 90% training success with 30.6% fewer transitions than Vanilla SAC and 34.1-35.1% fewer than current-state CBF-filtered SAC baselines. Across unseen simulated environments, SAFTER improves success by up to 42.4 and 61.4 percentage points over the state-of-the-art methods CBF-RL and SEA-Nav, respectively, and achieves 73.3% and 76.7% success on two real-world navigation maps. Ablations identify accurate differentiation through the safety filter as a key contributor to robustness, in which replacing the projection Jacobian with the identity approximation reduces success rate in a High-Shift environment from 61.4% to 6.2%. These results show that recoverability-aware filtering serves as both a runtime safety mechanism and a learning mechanism for sample-efficient, robust policies.
core_methodology: Uses Safety-Aware Filtering with differentiable Control Barrier Functions (CBF) for reinforcement learning under distribution shift
data_sources: Simulated and real-world quadruped navigation environments
alpha_potential: Limited direct financial application but may inspire risk-aware reinforcement learning approaches for automated trading systems

title: Same Probabilities, Different Advice: Gain-Loss Framing Effects in High-Stakes LLM Decision Support
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to support consequential decisions, yet their reliability under equivalent representations of uncertainty remains unclear. Existing work has documented prompt sensitivity, cognitive biases, and confidence miscalibration, but it is still unknown whether high-stakes advice changes when the same probability is expressed through complementary gain and loss frames. We introduce FrameBench-HPS, a controlled benchmark of 2,880 prompts derived from 240 high-stakes scenarios across healthcare, finance, education/career, and legal/consumer-rights domains. Across seven LLMs, gain-loss framing changes the recommendation category in 32.4% of complete groups, with most changes involving uncertainty rather than direct reversals. Human evaluation confirms corresponding shifts in perceived risk and directiveness. Robustness experiments show that framing effects persist under conversational paraphrases and exceed ordinary repeated-generation variability. Probability canonicalization substantially reduces framing sensitivity, identifying probability representation as a practical target for improving consistency in high-stakes LLM decision support.
core_methodology: Investigates framing effects in LLM decision support through controlled benchmarking
data_sources: Fictional high-stakes scenarios (including finance) from FrameBench-HPS benchmark
alpha_potential: Potential insights for improving decision consistency in LLM-based financial analytics

title: Latent space configuration for neural network finetuning, fast ranking, and embedding dimensionality reduction
summary: Finding K most similar elements for a query in a large gallery of neural network (NN) embeddings is essential in various areas of computer science and industrial applications of artificial intelligence. This paper proposes search algorithms for structured latent spaces (LS) of NNs which allow to speed up top K item retrieval owing to O(1) complexity small candidate gallery subset search. ArcFace-pretrained IResNet50 models are finetuned using Latent Space Configuration (LSC) methodology to obtain new distribution of embeddings with desired geometric properties. Applying the proposed algorithms to embeddings obtained from finetuned models leads to several times speed-up over baseline exhaustive search. Specifically, we report up to 3 times speed-up on GPU and 40% speed-up on CPU compared to the baseline method GPU speed. These results are obtained for the original and reduced numbers of LS dimensions. The results show that LS dimensionality reduction allows to further accelerate the search and even improve rank-N metrics.
core_methodology: Optimizing neural network latent spaces for fast similarity search through geometric configuration and dimensionality reduction
data_sources: Generic image embeddings (ArcFace-pretrained IResNet50) - no financial data used
alpha_potential: Potential efficiency improvements in similarity-based trading models (e.g., pattern recognition), but no demonstrated financial application

title: Harness Scaling for Generalizable Agentic Reinforcement Learning
summary: Agent harnesses have become a central component of modern agentic systems, shaping how models use tools, manage context, and coordinate long-horizon interaction. Realizing the benefits of these harnesses depends on how effectively the underlying model can make use of them, motivating reinforcement learning directly through the harness. However, existing approaches typically train through a single fixed harness, which can lead to specialization and limited transfer across harness configurations. To address this, we introduce \textbf{Harness Scaling}, a new scaling dimension for agentic RL that extends training from a single harness to diverse execution configurations. Concretely, we construct a factorized harness space, select a compact training subset with balanced factorial coverage, and organize cross-harness training to combine global coverage with controlled variation for the same task. Across multiple benchmarks, model scales, and RL algorithms, Harness Scaling consistently improves generalization to unseen white-box configurations. Moreover, models trained through structured white-box variation transfer effectively to unseen external black-box harnesses, outperforming models trained through a single complex black-box harness. These results establish harness diversity as a meaningful scaling dimension for agentic RL and highlight the importance of how this diversity is organized for cross-harness generalization.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Harness Scaling, a method for training agentic reinforcement learning models across diverse execution configurations to improve generalization.
data_sources: Not explicitly mentioned, but likely involves simulated environments or benchmarks for testing.
alpha_potential: Limited immediate applicability to trading; potential lies in improving generalizability of RL agents which could be adapted to financial markets.

title: Phase Transitions in Learning Driven by Extremal Data
summary: We study an extremal regression problem, an example of multiple instance learning (MIL), where the predictors are given as multisets, called bags. The bag elements (called instances) possess hidden labels which are pooled to produce an observed bag-level label. Max pooling is common in MIL applications, but gives rise to vanishing gradients. To handle this, modern MIL pipelines approximate the max with a softmax, treating the sharpness as a learnable parameter, denoted $\lambda$. When the max pooling model is the true data generating process, learning will be successful when $\lambda$ is increased during gradient descent, thereby driving the dynamics into regions of parameter space with vanishing gradients. To understand the conditions under which gradient descent breaks down, we study a minimal model and derive a low dimensional projection of the gradient flow in the joint limit of large bags $n$ and high dimension $d$ with $\alpha=\ln n/d$ fixed. The flow has two distinct phase transitions: an intrinsic freezing transition related to the random energy model of disordered systems, and a retrieval transition occurring in modern Hopfield networks. Numerical simulation confirms both the phase diagram and the convergence of the finite-size training gradient to its predicted asymptotic form.
